bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: =魏紀二=

translations.literal: = Wei Records 2 =
translations.idiomatic: Wei Records 2

sentences.zh: 起昭陽單閼，盡強圖協洽，凡五年。

translations.literal: Beginning with Zhaoyang Danqian, ending with Qiangtu Xiejia, five years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Wei Records 2] Spanning from the year Zhaoyang Danqian through Qiangtu Xiejia—a period of five years.

sentences.zh: 世祖文皇帝下

translations.literal: Founder Emperor Wen, Part Two (lower)
translations.idiomatic: The Reign of Emperor Wen the Founder, Part Two

sentences.zh: 1春，正月，曹真使張郃擊破吳兵，遂奪據江陵中洲。

translations.literal: 1. Spring, first month, Cao Zhen sent Zhang He to defeat Wu forces and then seized and held the central islet at Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: 1. In spring, during the first month, Cao Zhen dispatched Zhang He to rout the Wu army and then captured and held the central sandbank at Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 2二月，諸葛亮至永安。

translations.literal: 2. Second month, Zhuge Liang arrived at Yong'an.
translations.idiomatic: 2. In the second month, Zhuge Liang reached Yong'an.

sentences.zh: 3曹仁以步騎數萬向濡須，先揚聲欲東攻羨溪，朱桓分兵赴之。

translations.literal: 3. Cao Ren led infantry and cavalry numbering tens of thousands toward Ruxu, first spreading word that he intended to attack Xianxi to the east; Zhu Huan divided his forces to go there.
translations.idiomatic: 3. Cao Ren marched several ten thousands of foot and horse toward Ruxu, first giving out that he meant to strike east at Xianxi; Zhu Huan detached troops to meet him.

sentences.zh: 既行，仁以大軍徑進。

translations.literal: After they had set out, Ren advanced with his main force by the direct route.
translations.idiomatic: Once those detachments were on the road, Ren drove his main army straight ahead.

sentences.zh: 桓聞之，追還羨溪兵，兵未到而仁奄至。

translations.literal: When Huan heard of it, he recalled the Xianxi troops, but before the troops arrived Ren had already come upon them suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: Huan heard this and called back the Xianxi column, but Ren arrived in force before those troops could return.

sentences.zh: 時桓手下及所部兵在者才五千人，諸將業業各有懼心，桓喻之曰：「凡兩軍交對，勝負在將，不在眾寡。

translations.literal: At the time Huan had only about five thousand men under his own command and in his division who were present; the generals were all uneasy and fearful in heart. Huan instructed them, saying: "In any engagement between two armies, victory and defeat lie in the commander, not in whether forces are many or few.
translations.idiomatic: Huan then had only about five thousand men of his personal following and command still on hand; his officers were anxious and afraid. He addressed them: "When two armies meet, victory rests with the general, not with numbers.

sentences.zh: 諸君聞曹仁用兵行師，孰與桓邪？

translations.literal: You gentlemen have heard of Cao Ren's conduct in campaigning—is he a match for Huan?
translations.idiomatic: You have all heard how Cao Ren wages war—is he my equal?

sentences.zh: 兵法所以稱『客倍而主人半』者，謂俱在平原無城隍之守，又謂士卒勇怯齊等故耳。

translations.literal: The reason military theory speaks of 'the guest having twice the host's strength, while the host has but half' is that it assumes both are on level ground without walled defenses, and also that soldiers' courage and cowardice are equal.
translations.idiomatic: The manuals' line that 'the invader counts double while the defender counts for half' applies only when both fight on open plain without walled cover, and when courage and cowardice are evenly matched on both sides.

sentences.zh: 今仁既非智勇，加其士卒甚怯，又千里步涉，人馬罷困。

translations.literal: Now Ren is neither wise nor brave, and moreover his soldiers are very fearful; they have also marched on foot a thousand li, and men and horses are weary and exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Ren lacks both wisdom and dash, his men are thoroughly timid, and after a thousand li on foot both men and horses are worn out.

sentences.zh: 桓與諸君共據高城，南臨大江，北背山陵，以逸待勞，為主制客，此百戰百勝之勢，雖曹丕自來，尚不足憂，況仁等邪！

translations.literal: Huan and you gentlemen together hold a high city, south facing the great river, north backed by hills and ridges; awaiting the weary with the rested, as host controlling the guest—this is the posture of winning a hundred battles in a hundred; even if Cao Pi came in person, he would not be worth worry, how much less Ren and his sort!
translations.idiomatic: We hold a stronghold with the great Yangzi before us and hills at our backs, fresh troops against weary foes, defender mastering invader—every advantage of a position that wins a hundred fights in a hundred. Even Cao Pi himself need not worry us, let alone men like Ren!

sentences.zh: 」桓乃偃旗鼓，外示虛弱以誘致仁。

translations.literal: " Huan then lowered banners and drums, outwardly showing weakness to lure Ren.
translations.idiomatic: Huan then furled banners and silenced drums, feigning weakness to draw Ren in.

sentences.zh: 仁遣其子泰攻濡須城，分遣將軍常雕、王雙等乘油船別襲中洲。

translations.literal: Ren sent his son Tai to attack Ruxu city, and separately dispatched Generals Chang Diao, Wang Shuang, and others in oil-filled boats to make a separate strike at the central islet.
translations.idiomatic: Ren sent his son Tai against Ruxu fortress while detaching Generals Chang Diao, Wang Shuang, and others in fire ships for a separate assault on the central sandbank.

sentences.zh: 中洲者，桓部曲妻子所在也。

translations.literal: The central islet was where the wives and dependents of Huan's retainers were located.
translations.idiomatic: That sandbank was where the families of Huan's retainers were quartered.

sentences.zh: 蔣濟曰：「賊據西岸，列船上流，而兵入洲中，是為自內地獄，危亡之道也。

translations.literal: Jiang Ji said: "The rebels hold the west bank and line their boats upstream, while our troops enter the islet—this is to walk into a net of one's own making, the path to peril and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Ji said: "The enemy holds the western shore with boats lined upstream; to send troops onto the islet is to march into a trap they have set for themselves—the road to defeat.

sentences.zh: 」仁不從，自將萬人留橐皋，為泰等後援。

translations.literal: " Ren did not follow this advice; he personally led ten thousand men to remain at Tuogao as rear support for Tai and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Ren would not listen. He kept ten thousand men with him at Tuogao as a reserve for Tai's force.

sentences.zh: 桓遣別將擊雕等而身自拒泰，泰燒營退。

translations.literal: Huan sent a separate commander to strike Diao and the others while he personally resisted Tai; Tai burned his camp and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Huan sent a subordinate commander against Diao's column while he faced Tai himself; Tai burned his camps and pulled back.

sentences.zh: 桓遂斬常雕，生虜王雙，臨陳殺溺死者千餘人。

translations.literal: Huan then beheaded Chang Diao, captured Wang Shuang alive, and at the battlefront killed and drowned more than a thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Huan then executed Chang Diao, took Wang Shuang alive, and more than a thousand of the enemy were slain or drowned before the lines.

sentences.zh: 初，呂蒙病篤，吳王問曰：「卿如不起，誰可代者？

translations.literal: Earlier, when Lü Meng was gravely ill, the King of Wu asked: "If you cannot rise again, who can replace you?
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Lü Meng lay gravely ill, Sun Quan asked: "If you cannot recover, who could take your place?

sentences.zh: 」蒙對曰：「朱然膽守有餘，愚以為可任。

translations.literal: " Meng replied: "Zhu Ran has courage and strength in defense to spare; I, Meng, think he can be entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: " Meng answered: "Zhu Ran has more than enough nerve for defense; I believe he can bear the charge.

sentences.zh: 」朱然者，九真太守朱治姊子也；

translations.literal: " Zhu Ran was the son of Zhu Zhi's elder sister, Administrator of Jiuzhen;
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ran was the nephew of Zhu Zhi, prefect of Jiuzhen;

sentences.zh: 本姓施氏，治養以為子，時為昭武將軍。

translations.literal: his original surname was Shi; Zhi had raised him as a son, and at the time he was General Who Establishes Martial Might.
translations.idiomatic: born a Shi, he had been adopted by Zhi and was then General Who Establishes Martial Might.

sentences.zh: 蒙卒，吳王假然節，鎮江陵。

translations.literal: When Meng died, the King of Wu granted Ran command authority and stationed him at Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: After Meng died, Sun Quan gave Ran a staff of authority and posted him at Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 及曹真等圍江陵，破孫盛，吳王遣諸葛瑾等將兵往解圍，夏侯尚擊卻之。

translations.literal: When Cao Zhen and the others besieged Jiangling and defeated Sun Sheng, the King of Wu sent Zhuge Jin and other commanders with troops to relieve the siege; Xiahou Shang struck and drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Zhen and his colleagues encircled Jiangling and routed Sun Sheng, Sun Quan sent Zhuge Jin and others to break the siege; Xiahou Shang attacked and repulsed them.

sentences.zh: 江陵中外斷絕，城中兵多腫病，堪戰者裁五千人。

translations.literal: Inside and outside Jiangling communications were cut off; many soldiers in the city had swollen illnesses, and those fit to fight numbered barely five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangling was cut off within and without; many defenders were bloated with illness, and barely five thousand could still fight.

sentences.zh: 真等起土山，鑿地道，立樓櫓臨城，弓矢雨注，將士皆失色；

translations.literal: Zhen and the others raised earthen mounds, dug underground passages, set siege towers overlooking the walls, and arrows poured like rain; officers and soldiers all lost color;
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's men threw up earthworks, dug saps, and raised siege towers over the walls; arrows fell like rain and the garrison went pale;

sentences.zh: 然晏如無恐意，方厲吏士，伺間隙，攻破魏兩屯。

translations.literal: yet Ran was composed and without fear, and was just then exhorting clerks and warriors, watching for an opening, and broke two Wei camps.
translations.idiomatic: yet Ran remained serene and unafraid, urging his officers and men on and, seizing his chance, stormed two Wei camps.

sentences.zh: 魏兵圍然凡六月，江陵令姚泰領兵備城北門，見外兵盛，城中人少，穀食且盡，懼不濟，謀為內應，然覺而殺之。

translations.literal: Wei troops besieged Ran for six months in all. The magistrate of Jiangling, Yao Tai, commanded troops guarding the north gate; seeing the outer army strong, few people in the city, and grain nearly gone, he feared success would not come and plotted to act as an inside collaborator; Ran discovered this and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei invested Ran for six months altogether. Yao Tai, prefect of Jiangling, held the north gate with his troops; seeing the enemy strong, the city sparse, and grain nearly spent, he despaired of relief and plotted treason; Ran uncovered it and put him to death.

sentences.zh: 時江水淺狹，夏侯尚欲乘船將步騎入渚中安屯，作浮橋，南北往來，議者多以為城必可拔。

translations.literal: At the time the river was shallow and narrow; Xiahou Shang wished to embark infantry and cavalry in boats into the mid-stream shallows to establish camps, build a pontoon bridge, and pass to and fro north and south; those in council for the most part thought the city could certainly be taken.
translations.idiomatic: The river was then shallow and narrow; Xiahou Shang meant to ferry foot and horse into the shallows by boat, encamp there, span a floating bridge, and move forces north and south. Most advisers held that the city was sure to fall.

sentences.zh: 董昭上疏曰：「武皇帝智勇過人，而用兵畏敵，不敢輕之若此也。

translations.literal: Dong Zhao submitted a memorial, saying: "Martial Emperor Wu surpassed all others in wisdom and courage, yet in employing troops he feared the enemy and did not dare act lightly as this.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhao memorialized the throne: "Emperor Wu in martial wisdom outshone other men, yet he still feared the enemy and would not treat war lightly as we do now.

sentences.zh: 夫兵好進惡退，常然之數。

translations.literal: Troops love advance and hate retreat—that is their constant pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Armies love to advance and hate to retreat; that is their constant habit.

sentences.zh: 平地無險，猶尚艱難，就當深入，還道宜利，兵有進退，不可如意。

translations.literal: On level ground without danger it is still difficult; how much more when one must penetrate deeply—on the return route advantage should lie with oneself, yet troops advance and retreat and cannot have their will.
translations.idiomatic: Even on open ground without hazard the going is hard; how much more when one drives deep in—and the road back should favor the defender, yet movement cannot always be as one wishes.

sentences.zh: 今屯渚中，至深也；

translations.literal: Now encamping in the shallows is extreme depth;
translations.idiomatic: To camp now in the mid-river shallows is to go exceedingly deep;

sentences.zh: 浮橋而濟，至危也；

translations.literal: crossing on a floating bridge is extreme peril;
translations.idiomatic: to cross on a floating bridge is to court extreme peril;

sentences.zh: 一道而行，至狹也。

translations.literal: marching by a single route is extreme narrowness.
translations.idiomatic: to march on a single road is to face extreme constriction.

sentences.zh: 三者，兵家所忌，而今行之，賊頻攻橋，誤有漏失，渚中精銳非魏之有，將轉化為吳矣。

translations.literal: These three are what military families taboo, yet we are doing them now; if the rebels attack the bridge again and again, and through some slip the elite troops in the shallows will not belong to Wei but will turn into Wu's.
translations.idiomatic: All three are what strategists forbid, yet we do them now. If the enemy keeps hammering the bridge and a breach opens, the crack troops in the shallows will not remain Wei's—they will become Wu's.

sentences.zh: 臣私戚之，忘寢與食，而議者怡然不以為憂，豈不惑哉！

translations.literal: I privately am grieved, forgetting sleep and food, yet those in council are at ease and take no worry for it—can this not be delusion!
translations.idiomatic: I fret over this day and night, yet councils sit at ease and unmoved—is this not folly?

sentences.zh: 加江水向長，一旦暴增，何以防禦！

translations.literal: Moreover the river is trending toward rising; if it suddenly swells in flood, how can one defend against it!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the river is rising; should it burst in flood overnight, how could we stand against it?

sentences.zh: 就不破賊，尚當自完，奈何乘危，不以為懼！

translations.literal: Even if we do not defeat the rebels, we ought still to preserve ourselves—why ride danger and take no fear!
translations.idiomatic: Even failing to defeat the enemy we must still save ourselves—why court such danger without alarm?

sentences.zh: 惟陛下察之。

translations.literal: May Your Majesty examine this.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to weigh this carefully.

sentences.zh: 」帝即詔尚等促出，吳人兩頭並前，魏兵一道引去，不時得泄，僅而獲濟。

translations.literal: " The Emperor immediately ordered Shang and the others to withdraw quickly; Wu men advanced from both ends at once, and Wei troops withdrew along a single route and could not drain off in time, barely escaping across.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at once ordered Shang and the rest to hurry out. Wu pressed from both flanks while Wei filed off single-file and could not disperse in time—they barely got across.

sentences.zh: 吳將潘璋已作荻筏，欲以燒浮橋，會尚退而止。

translations.literal: Wu commander Pan Zhang had already built reed rafts intending to burn the floating bridge, but when Shang withdrew he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Wu general Pan Zhang had already built reed rafts to burn the bridge, but ceased when Shang withdrew.

sentences.zh: 後旬日，江水大漲，帝謂董昭曰：「君論此事，何其審也！

translations.literal: Some ten days later the river rose greatly, and the Emperor said to Dong Zhao: "Your discussion of this affair—how thorough it was!
translations.idiomatic: Ten days later the river rose sharply. The emperor told Dong Zhao: "How soundly you judged this matter!

sentences.zh: 」會天大疫，帝悉召諸軍還。

translations.literal: " Then a great pestilence spread through the heavens, and the Emperor recalled all armies.
translations.idiomatic: " A great plague then swept the land, and the emperor summoned every army home.

sentences.zh: 三月，丙申，車駕還洛陽。

translations.literal: Third month, on the day Bingshen, the imperial carriage returned to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the day Bingshen, the emperor's train returned to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 初，帝問賈詡曰：「吾欲伐不從命，以一天下，吳、蜀何先？

translations.literal: Earlier the Emperor asked Jia Xu: "I wish to attack those who do not obey commands to unite all under Heaven—which first, Wu or Shu?
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the emperor had asked Jia Xu: "I mean to chastise the disobedient and unite the realm—which should I strike first, Wu or Shu?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「攻取者先兵權，建本者尚德化。

translations.literal: " He replied: "He who attacks seizes military power first; he who builds the foundation esteems civil virtue.
translations.idiomatic: " Xu answered: "Conquest begins with seizing military advantage; founding a lasting order begins with civil virtue.

sentences.zh: 陛下應期受禪，撫臨率土，若綏之以文德而俟其變，則平之不難矣。

translations.literal: Your Majesty received the Mandate in season and rules all the land; if you soothe with civil virtue and await their transformation, pacifying them will not be difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty took the Mandate in its season and reigns over every quarter; if you soothe them with civil teaching and wait for change, their submission need not be hard.

sentences.zh: 吳、蜀雖蕞爾小國，依山阻水。

translations.literal: Wu and Shu, though tiny states no larger than gourds, lean on mountains and block the waters.
translations.idiomatic: Wu and Shu are but gourd-sized states, yet mountains and rivers shield them.

sentences.zh: 劉備有雄才，諸葛亮善治國；

translations.literal: Liu Bei has heroic talent, and Zhuge Liang is skilled at governing a state;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei has heroic stature; Zhuge Liang excels at governing;

sentences.zh: 孫權識虛實，陸遜見兵勢。

translations.literal: Sun Quan knows void and fullness, and Lu Xun perceives military situations.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan reads strength and weakness; Lu Xun reads the tide of war.

sentences.zh: 據險守要，泛舟江湖，皆難卒謀也。

translations.literal: Holding dangerous passes and guarding strategic points, floating boats on rivers and lakes—all are hard to take in a sudden stroke.
translations.idiomatic: They hold passes and sail the lakes and rivers—none of this yields to a hasty stroke.

sentences.zh: 用兵之道，先勝後戰，量敵論將；

translations.literal: The way of using troops is first to secure victory, then to fight; measure the foe and weigh the commander;
translations.idiomatic: The art of war is to secure victory before fighting, to weigh enemy and commander;

sentences.zh: 故舉無遺策。

translations.literal: thus no measure is raised without its plan succeeding.
translations.idiomatic: thus no plan is raised that is not already sure.

sentences.zh: 臣竊料群臣無備、權對，雖以天威臨之，未見萬全之勢也。

translations.literal: Your servant ventures to judge that among Your Majesty's ministers none could match Sun Quan; though you would bring Heaven's majesty against him, I do not see the posture of complete certainty.
translations.idiomatic: I judge that no minister of ours is Sun Quan's match; even Heaven's majesty brought against him offers no sure triumph.

sentences.zh: 昔舜舞干戚而有苗服，臣以為當今宜先文後武。

translations.literal: In antiquity Shun danced with shield and axe and the Miao submitted; I hold that today one should put civil measures first and martial measures after.
translations.idiomatic: When Shun danced with shield and axe the Miao bowed; I hold that today civil means should come first and arms after.

sentences.zh: 」帝不納，軍竟無功。

translations.literal: " The Emperor did not accept this, and the armies in the end achieved no merit.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not listen, and the campaigns came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 4丁未，陳忠侯曹仁卒。

translations.literal: 4. On the day Dingwei, Marquis of Loyalty and Sincerity Cao Ren died.
translations.idiomatic: 4. On the day Dingwei, Loyal and Sincere Marquis Cao Ren died.

sentences.zh: 5初，黃元為諸葛亮所不善，聞漢主疾病，懼有後患，故舉郡反，燒臨邛城。

translations.literal: 5. Earlier Huang Yuan had been ill regarded by Zhuge Liang; hearing that the Han Emperor was ill, he feared future trouble, and therefore raised the commandery in rebellion and burned Linqiong city.
translations.idiomatic: 5. Earlier Huang Yuan had fallen foul of Zhuge Liang. Hearing that the Han ruler was gravely ill, he feared what might follow and rebelled across the district, burning Linqiong.

sentences.zh: 時亮東行省疾，成都單虛，元益無所憚。

translations.literal: At the time Liang was traveling east to attend to the illness, Chengdu stood largely empty, and Yuan grew all the more brazen.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was then away east tending the emperor's illness; Chengdu lay nearly bare, and Yuan grew bolder.

sentences.zh: 益州治中從事楊洪，啟太子遣將軍陳曶、鄭綽討元。

translations.literal: Yang Hong, attendant administrator of Yizhou, notified the Crown Prince and dispatched Generals Chen Hu and Zheng Chuo to suppress Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hong, assistant administrator of Yizhou, alerted the crown prince and sent Generals Chen Hu and Zheng Chuo against Yuan.

sentences.zh: 眾議以為元若不能圍成都，當由越巂據南中。

translations.literal: The multitude in council held that if Yuan could not encircle Chengdu, he would pass through Yuexi and seize the southern interior.
translations.idiomatic: Most advisers thought that if Yuan could not take Chengdu he would head through Yuexi into the southern tribes.

sentences.zh: 洪曰：「元素性凶暴，無他恩信，何能辦此！

translations.literal: Hong said: "Yuan by nature is fierce and violent, without other kindness and trust—how could he accomplish this!
translations.idiomatic: Hong said: "Yuan is brutal by nature, with no other hold over men—how could he manage that?

sentences.zh: 不過乘水東下，冀主上平安，面縛歸死；

translations.literal: He would only ride the waters east, hoping the sovereign would be well and then come bound to die;
translations.idiomatic: He will only flee downriver, hoping the emperor recovers so he can bind himself and await death;

sentences.zh: 如其有異，奔吳求活耳。

translations.literal: if he has other intent, he will run to Wu to seek life.
translations.idiomatic: if not, he will flee to Wu for his life.

sentences.zh: 但敕曶、綽於南安峽口邀遮，即便得矣。

translations.literal: Only order Hu and Chuo to intercept at Nan'an Gorge, and he can be taken at once.
translations.idiomatic: Simply have Hu and Chuo ambush him at Nan'an Gorge and he is ours.

sentences.zh: 」元軍敗，果順江東下，曶、綽生獲，斬之。

translations.literal: " Yuan's army was defeated; he indeed went down the river east, and Hu and Chuo captured him alive and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was beaten and fled downriver as Hong had foretold; Hu and Chuo took him alive and executed him.

sentences.zh: 6漢主病篤，命丞相亮輔太子，以尚書令李嚴為副。

translations.literal: 6. The Han Emperor was gravely ill and ordered Chancellor Liang to assist the Crown Prince, with Director of the Secretariat Li Yan as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: 6. The Han emperor lay dying. He charged Chancellor Liang to assist the crown prince, with Li Yan, Director of the Secretariat, as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 漢主謂亮曰：「君才十倍曹丕，必能安國，終定大事。

translations.literal: The Han Emperor said to Liang: "Your talent is ten times that of Cao Pi; you will certainly be able to secure the state and in the end settle the great affair.
translations.idiomatic: He told Liang: "Your gifts outdo Cao Pi's tenfold; you can surely steady the state and bring our great cause to its end.

sentences.zh: 若嗣子可輔，輔之；

translations.literal: If the heir can be assisted, assist him;
translations.idiomatic: If the heir proves fit, assist him;

sentences.zh: 如其不才，君可自取。

translations.literal: if he lacks ability, you may take it for yourself.
translations.idiomatic: if he lacks ability, you may take the throne for yourself.

sentences.zh: 」亮涕泣曰：「臣敢不竭股肱之力，效忠貞之節，繼之以死！

translations.literal: " Liang wept and said: "Your servant dares not fail to exhaust the strength of arm and thigh, fulfill the fidelity of loyalty, and follow with death!
translations.idiomatic: Liang wept: "I shall spare neither limb nor life but serve with flawless loyalty till death!

sentences.zh: 」漢主又為詔敕太子曰：「人五十不稱夭，吾年已六十有餘，何所復恨，但以卿兄弟為念耳。

translations.literal: " The Han Emperor also drafted an edict instructing the Crown Prince: "A man is not called short-lived before fifty; I am already more than sixty, what more is there to regret—only that I think of you brothers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also wrote for the crown prince: "Fifty is not early death; I am past sixty and have little left to regret save concern for you and your brothers.

sentences.zh: 勉之，勉之！

translations.literal: Strive on, strive on!
translations.idiomatic: Strive hard, strive hard!

sentences.zh: 勿以惡小而為之，勿以善小而不為！

translations.literal: Do not do evil because it is small; do not leave good undone because it is small!
translations.idiomatic: Do not commit a small evil thinking it trivial; do not omit a small good thinking it worthless!

sentences.zh: 惟賢惟德，可以服人。

translations.literal: Only the worthy and the virtuous can win men's submission.
translations.idiomatic: Only worth and virtue can win men's hearts.

sentences.zh: 汝父德薄，不足效也。

translations.literal: Your father's virtue is thin and not worth imitating.
translations.idiomatic: Your father's virtue is meager—do not try to mimic me.

sentences.zh: 汝與丞相從事，事之如父。

translations.literal: You shall work with the Chancellor; serve him as a father.
translations.idiomatic: Work with the chancellor and serve him as you would a father.

translations.idiomatic: The first day of the fourth month was Jiji; there was no Guisi that month.

translations.idiomatic: The History of Shu's biography of the Former Lord records 'on the twenty-fourth of this month he passed away'; that day was Renwu, and the date is emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 丞相亮奉喪還成都，以李嚴為中都護，留鎮永安。

translations.literal: Chancellor Liang escorted the coffin back to Chengdu, appointed Li Yan as Central Supervisor of the Army, and left him to garrison Yong'an.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Liang brought the coffin back to Chengdu, made Li Yan Central Supervisor of the Army, and left him to hold Yong'an.

sentences.zh: 五月，太子禪即位，時年十七。

translations.literal: Fifth month, the Crown Prince Chan ascended the throne; he was seventeen years old.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Crown Prince Chan took the throne at the age of seventeen.

sentences.zh: 尊皇后曰皇太后，大赦，改元建興。

translations.literal: The Empress was honored as Empress Dowager; a general amnesty was declared; the era name was changed to Jianxing.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was elevated to empress dowager, a general amnesty was proclaimed, and the era name became Jianxing.

sentences.zh: 封丞相亮為武鄉侯，領益州牧，政事無鉅細，鹹決於亮。

translations.literal: Chancellor Liang was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wuxiang and appointed Governor of Yizhou; in government affairs great and small, all were decided by Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wuxiang and made governor of Yizhou; every matter of state, large or small, rested with him.

sentences.zh: 亮乃約官職，修法制，發教與群下曰：「夫參署者，集眾思，廣忠益也。

translations.literal: Liang then streamlined offices, revised laws and regulations, and issued an instruction to his subordinates, saying: "Participation in deliberation gathers many thoughts and broadens loyal benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Liang streamlined offices, revised the laws, and addressed his officials: "Deliberation in council gathers many minds and widens loyal counsel.

sentences.zh: 若遠小嫌，難相違覆，曠闕損矣。

translations.literal: If one keeps distant small resentments, it is hard to dispute and reconsider together, and broad omissions and harm result.
translations.idiomatic: If petty grudges keep men apart, frank debate fails and the state suffers for it.

sentences.zh: 違覆而得中，猶棄敝趫而獲珠玉。

translations.literal: To dispute and reconsider and hit the center is like discarding worn sandals and gaining pearls and jade.
translations.idiomatic: To argue back and forth and reach the right course is like throwing away worn shoes and finding pearls.

sentences.zh: 然人心苦不能盡，惟徐元直處茲不惑。

translations.literal: Yet men's hearts bitterly cannot go to the full; only Xu Yuanshi in this was not confused.
translations.idiomatic: Yet few can bring themselves to speak fully; only Xu Yuanshi never wavered on this point.

sentences.zh: 又，董幼宰參署七年，事有不至，至於十反，來相啟告。

translations.literal: Moreover Dong Youzai participated in deliberation for seven years; whenever matters did not reach completion, he would come up to ten times to inform and advise.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Youzai sat in council seven years; whenever something fell short he would come back as many as ten times to set me straight.

sentences.zh: 苟能慕元直之十一，幼宰之勤渠，有忠於國，則亮可以少過矣。

translations.literal: If you can emulate Yuanshi's one-tenth and Youzai's diligence and earnestness, being loyal to the state, then Liang can have fewer faults.
translations.idiomatic: If you will emulate even a tenth of Yuanshi's candor and Youzai's tireless honesty in serving the state, I may have fewer faults of my own.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「昔初交州平，屢聞得失；

translations.literal: " He also said: "In the past when I first associated with Zhou Ping, I repeatedly heard of gains and losses;
translations.idiomatic: He went on: "When I first knew Zhou Ping I often heard frank judgment of right and wrong;

sentences.zh: 後交元直，勤見啟誨；

translations.literal: later I associated with Yuanshi, who diligently came to enlighten and instruct;
translations.idiomatic: later I knew Xu Yuanshi, who often came with frank counsel;

sentences.zh: 前參事於幼宰，每言則盡；

translations.literal: earlier I deliberated with Youzai, and whenever he spoke he went to the full;
translations.idiomatic: before that Dong Youzai sat in council with me and never held back;

sentences.zh: 後從事於偉度，數有諫止。

translations.literal: later I worked with Weidu, who repeatedly admonished and restrained me.
translations.idiomatic: later Hu Ji served under me and often checked my course.

sentences.zh: 雖資性鄙暗，不能悉納，然與此四子終始好合，亦足以明其不疑於直言也。

translations.literal: Although my endowment is base and dim and I cannot fully accept all, yet with these four men I was in harmony from beginning to end, which is enough to show that I do not doubt frank speech.
translations.idiomatic: Though I am dull by nature and cannot take every word to heart, my lifelong goodwill with these four men shows I do not distrust honest speech.

sentences.zh: 」偉度者，亮主簿義陽胡濟也。

translations.literal: " Weidu was Liang's chief clerk Hu Ji of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Weidu was Hu Ji of Yiyang, Liang's chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 亮嘗自校簿書，主簿楊顒直入，諫曰：「為治有體，上下不可相侵。

translations.literal: Liang once personally checked account books; Chief Clerk Yang Yi entered directly and remonstrated, saying: "In governing there is a proper structure; superior and subordinate must not encroach on each other.
translations.idiomatic: Liang once audited the ledgers himself. Chief Clerk Yang Yi came straight in and said: "Government has its proper form; superiors and subordinates must not usurp one another's roles.

sentences.zh: 請為明公以作家譬之。

translations.literal: Allow me to illustrate for Your Excellency with a household.
translations.idiomatic: Let me put it in terms of running a household.

sentences.zh: 今有人，使奴執耕稼，婢典炊爨，雞主司晨，犬主吠盜，牛負重載，馬涉遠路。

translations.literal: Suppose a man has slaves tend the fields, maidservants manage the cooking, the cock announces dawn, the dog barks at thieves, oxen bear heavy loads, and horses travel distant roads.
translations.idiomatic: A man sets slaves to plow, maids to cook, the cock to wake the house, the dog to warn of thieves, oxen to haul burdens, and horses to travel far roads.

sentences.zh: 私業無曠，所求皆足，雍容高枕，飲食而已。

translations.literal: Private affairs are not neglected, all needs are met, and he sits at ease with head on pillow—eating and drinking, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Every task is done, every want supplied, and the master reclines at ease—eating and drinking, nothing more.

sentences.zh: 忽一旦盡欲以身親其役，不復付任，勞其體力，為此碎務，形疲神困，終無一成。

translations.literal: Suddenly one day he wishes to perform every task in person, no longer entrusting duties, exhausting his strength on these petty matters—body weary, spirit strained, and in the end achieving nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Then one day he insists on doing every chore himself, trusts no one, wears body and mind on trifles, and ends by accomplishing nothing.

sentences.zh: 豈其智之不如奴婢雞狗哉？

translations.literal: Is his intelligence not equal to that of slaves, maidservants, cock, and dog?
translations.idiomatic: Is he less wise than his slaves, maids, cock, and dog?

sentences.zh: 失為家主之法也。

translations.literal: This is to fail the method of being master of a household.
translations.idiomatic: That is to fail the art of being master of a house.

sentences.zh: 是故古人稱『坐而論道，謂之王公；

translations.literal: Therefore the ancients said, 'To sit and discuss the Way is called king or duke;
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said: 'To sit and discuss the Way is the work of kings and dukes;

sentences.zh: 作而行之，謂之士大夫。

translations.literal: to act and carry it out is called grandee or officer.'
translations.idiomatic: to act and carry it out is the work of officers.'

sentences.zh: 』故丙吉不問橫道死人而憂牛喘，陳平不肯知錢穀之數，云『自有主者』，彼誠達於位分之體也。

translations.literal: ' Therefore Bing Ji did not ask about a corpse in the crossroads but worried about an ox panting; Chen Ping refused to know the figures for money and grain, saying 'there are those in charge'—they truly understood the substance of rank and division.
translations.idiomatic: Bing Ji ignored a corpse in the road but fretted over a panting ox; Chen Ping would not learn the grain accounts, saying 'others have that charge'—both grasped what their stations required.

sentences.zh: 今明公為治，乃躬自校簿書，流汗終日，不亦勞乎！

translations.literal: Now Your Excellency in governing personally checks account books, sweating all day—is this not laborious!
translations.idiomatic: Yet Your Excellency governs by sweating over ledgers all day—is that not excessive toil?

sentences.zh: 」亮謝之。

translations.literal: " Liang thanked him.
translations.idiomatic: Liang thanked him.

sentences.zh: 及顒卒，亮垂泣三日。

translations.literal: When Yi died, Liang wept for three days.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi died, Liang mourned him with tears for three days.

sentences.zh: 7六月，甲戌，任城威王彰卒。

translations.literal: 7. Sixth month, on the day Jiaxu, King Wei of Rencheng Zhang died.
translations.idiomatic: 7. In the sixth month, on the day Jiaxu, King Wei of Rencheng, Cao Zhang, died.

sentences.zh: 8甲申，魏壽肅侯賈詡卒。

translations.literal: 8. On the day Jiashen, Solemn Marquis of Weishou Jia Xu died.
translations.idiomatic: 8. On the day Jiashen, Solemn Marquis Jia Xu of Weishou died.

sentences.zh: 9大水。

translations.literal: 9. Great flood.
translations.idiomatic: 9. Severe flooding.

sentences.zh: 10吳賀齊襲蘄春，虜太守晉宗以歸。

translations.literal: 10. Wu's He Qi raided Qichun and captured Administrator Jin Zong, bringing him back.
translations.idiomatic: 10. He Qi of Wu stormed Qichun and carried off Prefect Jin Zong.

sentences.zh: 11初，益州郡耆帥雍闓殺太守正昂，因士燮以求附於吳，又執太守成都張裔以與吳，吳以闓為永昌太守。

translations.literal: 11. Earlier the aged leader of Yizhou commandery Yong Kai killed Administrator Zheng Ang, and through Shi Xie sought to attach to Wu; he also seized Administrator of Chengdu Zhang Yi and gave him to Wu; Wu appointed Kai Administrator of Yongchang.
translations.idiomatic: 11. Earlier Yong Kai, a tribal elder of Yizhou, killed Prefect Zheng Ang and, through Shi Xie, sought Wu's protection; he also seized Zhang Yi, prefect of Chengdu, and handed him to Wu, which made Kai prefect of Yongchang.

sentences.zh: 永昌功曹呂凱、府丞王伉率吏士閉境拒守，闓不能進，使郡人孟獲誘扇諸夷，諸夷皆從之。

translations.literal: Yongchang Merit Officer Lü Kai and Assistant Wang Kang led clerks and warriors to close the borders and resist; Kai could not advance, and sent a man of the commandery Meng Huo to entice and incite the various tribes, and all the tribes followed.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Kai, merit officer of Yongchang, and Assistant Wang Kang shut the borders and held out; blocked, Kai sent Meng Huo to stir the tribes, and they all rose with him.

sentences.zh: 牂柯太守朱褒、越巂夷王高定皆叛應闓。

translations.literal: Administrator of Zangge Zhu Bao and King of the Yi of Yuexi Gao Ding both rebelled in response to Kai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Bao, prefect of Zangge, and Gao Ding, king of the Yi in Yuexi, both rebelled in Kai's cause.

sentences.zh: 諸葛亮以新遭大喪，皆撫而不討，務農殖穀，閉關息民，民安食足而後用之。

translations.literal: Zhuge Liang, because the state had newly suffered great mourning, soothed all and did not punish, devoting effort to farming and growing grain, closing the passes and resting the people—when the people were secure in food and full, then he would use them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang, fresh from national mourning, soothed rather than struck, pushed farming and grain stores, closed the passes, and let the people rest until they were fed and settled—only then would he call on them.

sentences.zh: 12秋，八月，丁卯，以廷尉鐘繇為太尉，治書執法高柔代為廷尉。

translations.literal: 12. Autumn, eighth month, on the day Dingmao, Court Commandant Zhong Yao was made Grand Commandant, and Director of Documents and Law Enforcement Gao Rou replaced him as Court Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: 12. In autumn, the eighth month, on the day Dingmao, Zhong Yao was made Grand Commandant and Gao Rou, director of documents and law, succeeded him as Court Commandant.

sentences.zh: 是時三公無事，又希與朝政，柔上疏曰：「公輔之臣，皆國之棟樑，民所具瞻，而置之三事，不使知政，遂各偃息養高，鮮有進納，誠非朝廷崇用大臣之義，大臣獻可替否之謂也。

translations.literal: At this time the Three Excellencies had no duties and rarely took part in court government. Rou submitted a memorial, saying: "Ministers who assist the ruler are all the state's pillars and beams, whom the people look up to together; yet they are placed in the Three Offices and not allowed to know government, and so each rests and cultivates loftiness, rarely offering proposals—this truly is not the court's meaning in honoring and employing great ministers, nor what great ministers mean by offering approval and substituting disapproval.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Excellencies then had little to do and seldom joined in rule. Rou memorialized: "These chief ministers are the state's pillars and the people's gaze; yet set in the Three Offices without a hand in policy, they retire to cultivate reputation and rarely advise—neither how a court should honor its great ministers nor how ministers should speak for or against policy.

sentences.zh: 古者刑政有疑，輒議於槐、棘之下。

translations.literal: In antiquity when punishments and government had doubts, deliberation was promptly held beneath the locust and jujube trees.
translations.idiomatic: In old times doubtful law was debated under the locust and jujube trees.

sentences.zh: 自今之後，朝有疑議及刑獄大事，宜數以咨訪三公。

translations.literal: From now on, when the court has doubtful deliberations and great matters of punishment and imprisonment, it is fitting frequently to consult and inquire of the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth doubtful policy and major criminal cases should often be referred to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 三公朝朔、望之日，又可特延入講論得失，博盡事情，庶有補起天聽，光益大化。

translations.literal: On the days of the new and full moon when the Three Excellencies attend court, they may also be specially summoned in to discuss gains and losses, broadly exhausting affairs—perhaps thereby mending and rousing Heaven's hearing and brightening and benefiting great transformation.
translations.idiomatic: On the new- and full-moon audiences they might also be summoned to debate policy in full, perhaps thereby sharpening the emperor's ear and advancing great reform.

sentences.zh: 」帝嘉納焉。

translations.literal: " The Emperor praised and accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and adopted the proposal.

sentences.zh: 13辛未，帝校獵於滎陽，遂東巡。

translations.literal: 13. On the day Xinwei, the Emperor conducted a hunting review at Xingyang and then made an eastern tour.
translations.idiomatic: 13. On the day Xinwei the emperor hunted at Xingyang and then toured east.

sentences.zh: 九月，甲辰，如許昌。

translations.literal: Ninth month, on the day Jiachen, he went to Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the day Jiachen, he proceeded to Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 14漢尚書義陽鄧芝言於諸葛亮曰：「今主上幼弱，初即尊位，宜遣大使重申吳好。

translations.literal: 14. Han Director of the Secretariat Deng Zhi of Yiyang said to Zhuge Liang: "Now the sovereign is young and weak, having just assumed the honored position; it is fitting to send a great envoy to reaffirm friendship with Wu.
translations.idiomatic: 14. Deng Zhi of Yiyang, director of the secretariat, told Zhuge Liang: "The throne is young and newly filled; we should send a senior envoy to renew our bond with Wu.

sentences.zh: 」亮曰：「吾思之久矣，未得其人耳，今日始得之。

translations.literal: " Liang said: "I have thought on this long, but had not found the man; today I have found him.
translations.idiomatic: Liang said: "I have sought the right man a long while; today I have found him.

sentences.zh: 」芝問：「其人為誰？

translations.literal: " Zhi asked: "Who is the man?
translations.idiomatic: Zhi asked: "Who is he?

sentences.zh: 」亮曰：「即使君也。

translations.literal: " Liang said: "It is you, sir.
translations.idiomatic: Liang said: "You, sir.

sentences.zh: 」乃遣芝以中郎將修好於吳。

translations.literal: " He then sent Zhi as General of the Gentlemen of the Household to establish good relations with Wu.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Zhi as a household general to treat with Wu.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，芝至吳。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, Zhi arrived in Wu.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, Zhi reached Wu.

sentences.zh: 時吳王猶未與魏絕，狐疑，不時見芝。

translations.literal: At the time the King of Wu had not yet broken with Wei and was hesitant, not receiving Zhi promptly.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan had not yet broken with Wei and hesitated, delaying Zhi's audience.

sentences.zh: 芝乃自表請見曰：「臣今來，亦欲為吳，非但為蜀也。

translations.literal: Zhi then submitted a memorial requesting audience, saying: "Your servant has come now also wishing to act for Wu, not only for Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi petitioned for an audience: "I come now to serve Wu's interest as much as Shu's.

sentences.zh: 」吳王見之，曰：「孤誠願與蜀和親，然恐蜀主幼弱，國小勢逼，為魏所乘，不自保全耳。

translations.literal: " The King of Wu received him and said: "I truly wish to ally in marriage with Shu, yet I fear the Shu sovereign is young and weak, the state small and pressed by circumstance, and will be ridden by Wei and unable to preserve itself.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan received him and said: "I truly wish kinship with Shu, yet I fear your young ruler, your small state pressed by power, will be overrun by Wei and cannot stand alone.

sentences.zh: 」芝對曰：「吳、蜀二國，四州之地。

translations.literal: " Zhi replied: "Wu and Shu are two states spanning four provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi answered: "Wu and Shu hold four provinces between them.

sentences.zh: 大王命世之英，諸葛亮亦一時之傑也；

translations.literal: Great King, a hero of the age; Zhuge Liang also a outstanding man of the time;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is a hero of the age; Zhuge Liang is a genius of his time;

sentences.zh: 蜀有重險之固，吳有三江之阻。

translations.literal: Shu has the security of layered peril, Wu has the barrier of the three rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Shu has its mountain fastnesses; Wu its three rivers.

sentences.zh: 合此二長，共為脣齒，進可並兼天下，退可鼎足而立，此理之自然也。

translations.literal: Join these two strengths, become lip and teeth together—advancing, you can unite and take all under Heaven; retreating, you can stand as a tripod of three legs. This is the natural reason of things.
translations.idiomatic: Join those strengths and you are lip to teeth: advance and you may unite the realm; retreat and you still stand as one leg of a tripod. That is nature's logic.

sentences.zh: 大王今若委質於魏，魏必上望大王之入朝，下求太子之內侍，若不從命，則奉辭伐叛，蜀亦順流見可而進。

translations.literal: If Great King now submits quality to Wei, Wei will above expect Great King to enter court and below demand the heir as inner attendant; if you do not follow the command, they will offer words to attack rebellion, and Shu also will go with the current and advance when it sees opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: If you now submit to Wei, they will demand your court attendance and your heir as hostage; refuse, and they march south under a punitive banner while Shu follows the river wherever chance opens.

sentences.zh: 如此，江南之地非復大王之有也。

translations.literal: Thus the lands south of the river will no longer belong to Great King.
translations.idiomatic: Then the lands south of the Yangzi will no longer be yours.

sentences.zh: 」吳王默然良久曰：「君言是也。

translations.literal: " The King of Wu was silent a long while and said: "Your words are right.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan was silent a long while, then said: "You are right.

sentences.zh: 」遂絕魏，專與漢連和。

translations.literal: " He then broke with Wei and allied exclusively with Han.
translations.idiomatic: He broke with Wei and allied solely with Han.

sentences.zh: 15是歲，漢主立妃張氏為皇后。

translations.literal: 15. This year the Han sovereign established Consort Zhang as Empress.
translations.idiomatic: 15. That year the Han emperor made Lady Zhang empress.

translations.literal: 1. Spring, second month <ref>Second month: according to Zhang's collation and the Annals of Emperor Wen in the History of Wei, both read 'third month.'
translations.idiomatic: 1. In spring, the second month. Note: Zhang's collation and the Wei Annals of Emperor Wen both read third month.

translations.literal: </ref>, the Emperor returned from Xuchang to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor returned from Xuchang to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 2初平以來，學道廢墜。

translations.literal: 2. Since the Chuping era, the path of learning has lain in ruins.
translations.idiomatic: 2. Since the Chuping era scholarship had collapsed.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，初立太學；

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, the Imperial Academy was first established;
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, the Imperial Academy was founded;

sentences.zh: 置博士，依漢制設《五經》課試之法。

translations.literal: Erudites were appointed, and following Han institutions the method of examination on the Five Classics was established.
translations.idiomatic: erudites were appointed and Han-style examinations on the Five Classics instituted.
