sentences.zh: 時事所宜，吳主常令陸遜語諸葛亮；

translations.literal: On timely matters the King of Wu often had Lu Xun speak with Zhuge Liang;
translations.idiomatic: On current affairs Sun Quan often had Lu Xun confer with Zhuge Liang;

sentences.zh: 又刻印置遜所，王每與漢主及諸葛亮書，常過示遜，輕重、可否有所不安，每令改定，以印封之。

translations.literal: he also carved a seal and placed it with Xun; whenever the King wrote to the Han sovereign and Zhuge Liang, he would pass it to Xun first; if weight or approval and disapproval were unsettled, he would have it revised and sealed with the stamp.
translations.idiomatic: and kept a seal with Xun. Letters to the Han emperor and Zhuge Liang passed through Xun first; if tone or policy seemed off, Sun had them revised and sealed.

sentences.zh: 漢復遣鄧芝聘於吳，吳主謂之曰：「若天下太平，二主分治，不亦樂乎？

translations.literal: Han again sent Deng Zhi on a mission of courtesy to Wu; the King of Wu said to him: "If all under Heaven were at peace and the two rulers divided governance, would that not also be joy?
translations.idiomatic: Han sent Deng Zhi again on a courtesy mission. Sun Quan said to him: "If the realm were at peace and our two thrones shared rule, would that not be pleasant?

sentences.zh: 」芝對曰：「天無二日，土無二王。

translations.literal: " Zhi replied: "Heaven has no two suns; earth has no two kings.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi answered: "Heaven admits but one sun; earth but one king.

sentences.zh: 如並魏之後，大王未深識天命，君各茂其德，臣各盡其忠，將提枹鼓，則戰爭方始耳。

translations.literal: After uniting with Wei, if Great King has not deeply recognized Heaven's Mandate, and each ruler cultivates his virtue while each minister exhausts his loyalty, and they raise drum and mallet—then war has only just begun.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wei is gone, if you have not read Heaven's Mandate aright, and each throne and each minister plays his part to the full, then the drums of war will sound and the fighting begin anew.

sentences.zh: 」吳王大笑曰：「君之誠款乃當爾邪！

translations.literal: " The King of Wu laughed greatly and said: "Your honest sincerity is truly thus!
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan laughed aloud: "Your candor is exactly what I hoped for!

sentences.zh: 4秋，七月，帝東巡，如許昌。

translations.literal: 4. Autumn, seventh month, the Emperor made an eastern tour and went to Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: 4. In autumn, the seventh month, the emperor toured east to Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 帝欲大興軍伐吳，侍中辛毗諫曰：「方今天下新定，土廣民稀，而欲用之，臣誠未見其利也。

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to raise armies on a great scale to attack Wu; Attendant-in-Ordinary Xin Pi remonstrated, saying: "Just now all under Heaven is newly settled, the land broad and the people sparse; yet you wish to use them—I truly do not see the profit.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor meant to raise a great host against Wu. Xin Pi remonstrated: "The realm is newly settled, land vast and people thin; to spend them now—I see no gain.

sentences.zh: 先帝屢起銳師，臨江而旋。

translations.literal: The Former Emperor repeatedly raised sharp armies, came to the river, and turned back.
translations.idiomatic: Your father repeatedly marched elite troops to the river and turned back.

sentences.zh: 今六軍不增於故，而復循之，此未易也。

translations.literal: Now the Six Armies are no greater than before, yet you would follow the same course—this is not easy.
translations.idiomatic: The Six Armies are no larger than before, yet you would repeat the attempt—that will not be easy.

sentences.zh: 今日之計，莫若養民屯田，十年然後用之，則役不再舉矣。

translations.literal: Today's plan is none better than nourishing the people and garrison-farming; use them only after ten years, and corvée will not be raised again.
translations.idiomatic: Better to nourish the people and farm garrison lands, and only after ten years call on them—then levies need not be repeated.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「如卿意，更當以虜遺子孫邪？

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "By your thinking, am I to leave the barbarians as a legacy to my descendants?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "By your counsel, am I to bequeath the enemy to my sons?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「昔周文王以紂遺武王，惟知時也。

translations.literal: " He replied: "In antiquity King Wen of Zhou left Zhou for King Wu—it was only knowing the season.
translations.idiomatic: Pi answered: "King Wen of Zhou left Zhou for King Wu—that was knowing the season.

sentences.zh: 」帝不從，留尚書僕射司馬懿鎮許昌。

translations.literal: " The Emperor did not follow this; he left Vice Director of the Secretariat Sima Yi to garrison Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not listen and left Sima Yi, vice director of the secretariat, to hold Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 八月，為水軍，親御龍舟，循蔡、潁，浮淮如壽春。

translations.literal: Eighth month, he formed a water army, personally manned the dragon boat, followed the Cai and Ying rivers, and floated on the Huai toward Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he built a fleet, boarded the imperial dragon boat, followed the Cai and Ying, and sailed the Huai toward Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 九月，至廣陵。

translations.literal: Ninth month, he reached Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he reached Guangling.

sentences.zh: 吳安東將軍徐盛建計，植木衣葦，為疑城假樓，自石頭至於江乘，聯綿相接數百里，一夕而成；

translations.literal: Wu General Who Pacifies the East Xu Sheng devised a plan: planting trees and clothing them with reeds to make false walls and mock towers, from Shitou to Jiangcheng, linked in unbroken succession for several hundred li, completed in one night;
translations.idiomatic: Xu Sheng of Wu devised a ruse: trees dressed in reeds to mimic walls and towers from Shitou to Jiangcheng, an unbroken line hundreds of li long, finished in a single night;

sentences.zh: 又大浮舟艦於江。

translations.literal: they also launched great floating warships on the river.
translations.idiomatic: and launched great war junks on the river.

sentences.zh: 時江水盛長，帝臨望，嘆曰：「魏雖有武騎千群，無所用之，未可圖也。

translations.literal: At the time the river was swollen and long; the Emperor looked out and sighed: "Though Wei has a thousand groups of martial cavalry, there is no use for them—Wu cannot be plotted against.
translations.idiomatic: The river ran high. The emperor gazed out and sighed: "Though Wei fields thousands of horsemen, they are useless here—Wu cannot be taken.

sentences.zh: 」帝御龍舟，會暴風漂蕩，幾至覆沒。

translations.literal: " The Emperor manned the dragon boat; a sudden gale arose and it drifted and tossed, nearly capsizing.
translations.idiomatic: Aboard his dragon boat a sudden gale nearly swamped him.

sentences.zh: 帝問群臣：「權當自來否？

translations.literal: The Emperor asked his ministers: "Will Quan come in person?
translations.idiomatic: He asked his ministers: "Will Sun Quan come himself?

sentences.zh: 」咸曰：「陛下親征，權恐怖，必舉國而應。

translations.literal: " All said: "Your Majesty campaigns in person; Quan will be terrified and must mobilize the whole state to respond.
translations.idiomatic: All said: "With Your Majesty in the field, Quan will be terrified and must answer with his whole state.

sentences.zh: 又不敢以大眾委之臣下，必當自來。

translations.literal: He also dares not entrust the great host to subordinates and must come in person.
translations.idiomatic: Nor will he trust his main force to a subordinate—he must come himself.

sentences.zh: 」劉曄曰：「彼謂陛下欲以萬乘之重牽己，而超越江湖者在於別將，必勒兵待事，未有進退也。

translations.literal: " Liu Ye said: "He thinks Your Majesty wishes to draw him out with the weight of ten thousand chariots, while the one who crosses rivers and lakes will be another commander—he is sure to hold his troops and await events, with neither advance nor retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ye said: "He will think Your Majesty means to lure him with imperial weight while another general crosses the river—he will hold his army and wait, neither advancing nor retreating.

sentences.zh: 」大駕停住積日，吳王不至，帝乃旋師。

translations.literal: " The imperial train halted many days; the King of Wu did not come, and the Emperor then turned the army.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial train waited many days; Sun Quan never came, and the emperor withdrew.

sentences.zh: 是時，曹休表得降賊辭：「孫權已在濡須口。

translations.literal: At this time Cao Xiu memorialized that he had obtained words from a surrendered rebel: "Sun Quan is already at Ruxukou.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Xiu then reported words from a defector: "Sun Quan is already at Ruxukou.

sentences.zh: 」中領軍衛臻曰：「權恃長江，未敢亢衡，此必畏怖偽辭耳！

translations.literal: " Central Army Commander Wei Zhen said: "Quan relies on the long river and dares not contend as equals—this must be frightened false words!
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhen, central army commander, said: "Quan trusts the Yangzi and dares not meet us head-on—this is surely a frightened lie!

sentences.zh: 」考核降者，果守將所作也。

translations.literal: " Investigating the surrenderer, it was indeed made by a garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: Investigation proved the defector was a garrison officer's plant.

sentences.zh: 5吳張溫少以俊才有盛名，顧雍以為當今無輩，諸葛亮亦重之。

translations.literal: 5. Wu's Zhang Wen in youth had great fame for outstanding talent; Gu Yong held that in the present age he had no peer, and Zhuge Liang also esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: 5. Zhang Wen of Wu won early fame for brilliance; Gu Yong called him peerless, and Zhuge Liang esteemed him too.

sentences.zh: 溫薦引同郡暨艷為選部尚書。

translations.literal: Wen recommended and introduced Ji Yan of his same commandery as Director of the Selection Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Wen recommended his townsman Ji Yan as director of the selection bureau.

sentences.zh: 艷好為清議，彈射百僚，覈奏三署，率皆貶高就下，降損數等，其守故者，十未能一；

translations.literal: Yan loved to make pure judgments, impeaching the hundred officials and auditing the Three Bureaus; for the most part he demoted the high and promoted the low, reducing rank by several grades—those who kept their former posts, not one in ten;
translations.idiomatic: Yan loved moralistic verdicts, impeaching officials and auditing the three bureaus; he mostly demoted the lofty and promoted the humble, cutting ranks by several grades—barely one in ten kept his post;

sentences.zh: 其居位貪鄙，志節污卑者，皆以為軍吏，置營府以處之；

translations.literal: those who held office with greed and baseness, whose will and integrity were filthy and low, he all made military clerks and placed in camp offices to house them;
translations.idiomatic: the greedy and base he turned into camp clerks and lodged in military offices;

sentences.zh: 多揚人闇昧之失以顯其謫。

translations.literal: he often broadcast men's hidden and obscure faults to display their demotions.
translations.idiomatic: and publicized men's hidden faults to justify their fall.

sentences.zh: 同郡陸遜、遜弟瑁及侍御史朱據皆諫止之。

translations.literal: Lu Xun of the same commandery, Xun's younger brother Mao, and Attending Censor Zhu Ju all remonstrated and stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun, his brother Mao, and censor Zhu Ju all urged him to stop.

sentences.zh: 瑁與艷書曰：「夫聖人嘉善矜愚，忘過記功，以成美化。

translations.literal: Mao wrote to Yan, saying: "The sage commends the good and pities the foolish, forgets faults and records merit, to accomplish beautiful transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Mao wrote to Yan: "Sages praise the good, pity the foolish, forget faults and record merit—that is how order is beautified.

sentences.zh: 如今王業始建，將一大統，此乃漢高棄瑕錄用之時也。

translations.literal: Now the royal enterprise is just being established and about to achieve great unification—this is the time when Han Gaozu discarded flaws and recorded employment.
translations.idiomatic: Our royal enterprise is newly founded and aims at great unification—this is the hour when Gaozu of Han overlooked flaws and put men to use.

sentences.zh: 若令善惡異流，貴汝、潁月旦之評，誠可以厲俗明教，然恐未易行也。

translations.literal: If one makes good and evil flow in separate channels, honoring the monthly appraisals of Runan and Ying, that truly could reform custom and clarify teaching—yet I fear it would not be easy to carry out.
translations.idiomatic: If you separate the worthy from the unworthy and honor the monthly appraisals made famous in Runan and Ying, that could indeed reform custom and clarify moral teaching—but I fear it would not be easily done.

sentences.zh: 宜遠模仲尼之泛愛，近則郭泰之容濟，庶有益於大道也。

translations.literal: One ought to take as a distant model Confucius's universal love, and as a nearer one Guo Tai's tolerant assistance—perhaps that would benefit the Great Way.
translations.idiomatic: Better to take Confucius's universal charity as a distant model and Guo Tai's tolerant generosity as a nearer one—perhaps then you would truly serve the greater good.

sentences.zh: 」據謂艷曰：「天下未定，舉清厲濁，足以沮勸；

translations.literal: " Ju said to Yan: "The empire is not yet settled; to exalt the pure and condemn the corrupt is enough to deter and encourage;
translations.idiomatic: Ju said to Yan, "The realm is not yet settled; to exalt the upright and restrain the corrupt is enough to deter wrongdoing and encourage virtue;

sentences.zh: 若一時貶黜，懼有後咎。

translations.literal: if one dismisses and demotes all at once, I fear there will be troubles afterward.
translations.idiomatic: but if you dismiss and demote men all at once, I fear there will be trouble later.

sentences.zh: 」艷皆不聽。

translations.literal: " Yan heeded none of it.
translations.idiomatic: But Yan would not listen to any of them.

sentences.zh: 於是怨憤盈路，爭言艷及選曹郎徐彪專用私情，憎愛不由公理。

translations.literal: Thereupon resentment filled the roads; many said Yan and Selection Bureau Clerk Xu Biao used private feelings exclusively—their hatred and favor did not follow public principle.
translations.idiomatic: Soon resentment filled the streets, and many complained that Yan and Xu Biao, clerk of the selection bureau, indulged private likes and dislikes rather than acting on public principle.

sentences.zh: 艷、彪皆坐自殺。

translations.literal: Yan and Biao both, on account of their crimes, committed suicide.
translations.idiomatic: Yan and Biao were both convicted and took their own lives.

sentences.zh: 溫素與艷、彪同意，亦坐斥還本郡以給廝吏，卒於家。

translations.literal: Wen had long shared the views of Yan and Biao; he too, on account of his crime, was dismissed and sent back to his home commandery to serve as a clerk, and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Wen had long shared the views of Yan and Biao; he too was convicted, dismissed, and sent back to his home commandery to serve as a clerical attendant, and he died at home.

sentences.zh: 始，溫方盛用事，餘姚虞俊嘆曰：「張惠恕才多智少，華而不實，怨之所聚，有覆家之禍。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Wen was at the height of power, Yu Jun of Yuyao sighed and said: "Zhang Hui-shu has much talent but little wisdom—glorious but not substantial; where resentment gathers, there is the calamity of overturning the family.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Wen was at the height of his power, Yu Jun of Yuyao remarked, "Zhang Hui-shu has much talent but little wisdom—splendid in appearance but insubstantial. Where resentment gathers, a family will be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 吾見其兆矣。

translations.literal: I see the signs of it already."
translations.idiomatic: I can already see the signs."

sentences.zh: 」無幾何而敗。

translations.literal: " Before long he fell.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, this came to pass.

sentences.zh: 6冬，十月，帝還許昌。

translations.literal: 6. Winter, tenth month, the Emperor returned to Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: 6. In the tenth month of winter, the Emperor returned to Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 7十一月，戊申晦，日有食之。

translations.literal: 7. Eleventh month, on the last day Wushen, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: 7. In the eleventh month, on the last day of the month, the day Wushen, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 8鮮卑軻比能誘步度根兄扶羅韓殺之，步度根由是怨軻比能，更相攻擊。

translations.literal: 8. The Xianbei leader Kebineng enticed Fuluohan, elder brother of Budugen, to kill him; Budugen therefore resented Kebineng, and they attacked each other in turn.
translations.idiomatic: 8. The Xianbei leader Kebineng induced Fuluohan, elder brother of Budugen, to kill him; Budugen thereupon turned against Kebineng, and the two attacked each other repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 步度根部眾稍弱，將其眾萬餘落保太原、雁門；

translations.literal: Budugen's tribal following grew somewhat weaker; he led more than ten thousand households to hold Taiyuan and Yanmen;
translations.idiomatic: Budugen's following grew weaker, and he led more than ten thousand households to take refuge in Taiyuan and Yanmen;

sentences.zh: 是歲，詣闕貢獻。

translations.literal: that year he went to the court to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: that year he went to court and presented tribute.

sentences.zh: 而軻比能眾遂強盛，出擊東部大人素利。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Kebineng's following grew strong; he went out to attack the Eastern Warchief Suli.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Kebineng's following grew strong, and he marched out to attack the Eastern Warchief Suli.

sentences.zh: 護烏丸校尉田豫乘虛掎其後，軻比能使別帥瑣奴拒豫，豫擊破之。

translations.literal: Protector of the Wuhuan Tian Yu seized the moment and struck from behind; Kebineng sent a separate commander Suonu to oppose Yu, and Yu defeated and broke him.
translations.idiomatic: Protector of the Wuhuan Tian Yu seized the moment and struck from behind; Kebineng sent a subordinate commander, Suonu, to hold Yu off, but Yu routed him.

sentences.zh: 軻比能由是攜貳，數為邊寇，幽、并苦之。

translations.literal: Kebineng from this harbored divided loyalties and repeatedly made border raids; You and Bing suffered from it.
translations.idiomatic: From this Kebineng grew disloyal and repeatedly raided the frontier, to the great distress of You and Bing provinces.

sentences.zh: 1春，二月，詔以陳群為鎮軍大將軍，隨車駕董督眾軍，錄行尚書事；

translations.literal: 1. Spring, second month, an edict appointed Chen Qun General Who Guards the Army, to accompany the imperial chariot in supervising all armies and to hold acting authority over the Masters of Writing;
translations.idiomatic: 1. In spring, during the second month, an edict appointed Chen Qun General Who Guards the Army, to accompany the imperial procession in supervising all armies and to hold acting authority over the Masters of Writing;

sentences.zh: 司馬懿為撫軍大將軍，留許昌，督後臺文書。

translations.literal: Sima Yi was made General Who Pacifies the Army, remaining at Xuchang to supervise the rear-office documents.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi was appointed General Who Pacifies the Army and remained at Xuchang to supervise the rear-office documents.

sentences.zh: 三月，帝行如召陵，通討虜渠；

translations.literal: Third month, the Emperor traveled to Zhaoling and cleared the Taonu Canal;
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, the Emperor traveled to Zhaoling and cleared the Taonu Canal;

sentences.zh: 乙巳，還許昌。

translations.literal: on the day Yisi he returned to Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Yisi he returned to Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 2并州刺史梁習討軻比能，大破之。

translations.literal: 2. Inspector of Bingzhou Liang Xi attacked Kebineng and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: 2. Liang Xi, Inspector of Bing Province, attacked Kebineng and inflicted a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 3漢諸葛亮率眾討雍闓等，參軍馬謖送之數十里。

translations.literal: 3. Han's Zhuge Liang led an army to attack Yong Kai and the others; Staff Officer Ma Su escorted him for several tens of li.
translations.idiomatic: 3. Zhuge Liang of Han led an army to attack Yong Kai and the others; Staff Officer Ma Su escorted him for several tens of li.

sentences.zh: 亮曰：「雖共謀之歷年，今可更惠良規。

translations.literal: Liang said: "Though we have plotted together for years, today you may offer me good counsel anew.
translations.idiomatic: Liang said, "Though we have plotted together for years, offer me your best counsel now.

sentences.zh: 」謖曰：「南中恃其險遠，不服久矣。

translations.literal: " Su said: "The south rests on its dangers and distance; it has long refused submission.
translations.idiomatic: Su said, "The south has long rested on its rugged terrain and distance and refused to submit.

sentences.zh: 雖今日破之，明日復反耳。

translations.literal: Even if we defeat them today, tomorrow they will rebel again.
translations.idiomatic: Even if we crush them today, they will rebel again tomorrow.

sentences.zh: 今公方傾國北伐以事強賊，彼知官勢內虛，其叛亦速。

translations.literal: Now Your Excellency is about to commit the whole state's strength to a northern expedition against a powerful foe; they will know the government's power is hollow within, and their rebellion will come quickly too.
translations.idiomatic: You are about to commit the realm's full strength to a northern expedition against a powerful enemy; when they see the government weakened at home, they will rebel all the sooner.

sentences.zh: 若殄盡遺類以除後患，既非仁者之情，且又不可倉卒也。

translations.literal: If we exterminate every survivor to remove future trouble, that is neither the sentiment of the benevolent man, and moreover it cannot be done in haste.
translations.idiomatic: To exterminate every survivor in order to remove future trouble would be unworthy of a benevolent man, and in any case it cannot be done in haste.

sentences.zh: 夫用兵之道，攻心為上，攻城為下，心戰為上，兵戰為下，願公服其心而已。

translations.literal: In the way of employing troops, to attack the heart is highest, to storm cities is lower; heart-battle is highest, troop-battle is lower—I wish Your Excellency would only make them submit in heart.
translations.idiomatic: In warfare, winning hearts comes first and storming cities second; fighting with minds ranks above fighting with arms. I hope you will conquer their hearts and no more.

sentences.zh: 」亮納其言。

translations.literal: " Liang accepted his words.
translations.idiomatic: Liang accepted his counsel.

sentences.zh: 謖，良之弟也。

translations.literal: Su was the younger brother of Ma Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Su was the younger brother of Ma Liang.

sentences.zh: 4辛未<ref>辛未是年三月戊寅朔，無辛未。

translations.literal: 4. On the day Xinwei<ref>On Xinwei: that year's third month had Wuyin as new moon—there was no Xinwei day.
translations.idiomatic: 4. On the day Xinwei. Editorial note: In the third month of this year the new moon fell on Wuyin; there was no day Xinwei.

sentences.zh: 疑為閏三月事，按閏三月戊申朔，為二十四日。

translations.literal: It is suspected to belong to the intercalary third month; according to the intercalary third month, Wushen as new moon, that would be the twenty-fourth day.
translations.idiomatic: This is suspected to refer to the intercalary third month; taking the intercalary third month's new moon on Wushen, that would be the twenty-fourth day.

sentences.zh: </ref>，帝以舟師復征吳，群臣大議，宮正鮑勳諫曰：「王師屢征而未有所克者，蓋以吳、蜀脣齒相依，憑阻山水，有難拔之勢故也。

translations.literal: </ref>, the Emperor with a naval force again attacked Wu; the ministers held great debate; Director of the Palace Bao Xun remonstrated, saying: "The royal army has repeatedly campaigned yet achieved no victory—this is because Wu and Shu are like lip and teeth, relying on mountains and rivers as barriers, with a momentum hard to uproot.
translations.idiomatic: [End editorial note.] The Emperor led a naval force against Wu again. The ministers debated the matter at length, and Bao Xun, Director of the Palace, remonstrated, "The royal army has campaigned many times without victory largely because Wu and Shu stand like lip and teeth, protected by mountains and rivers in positions that are hard to uproot.

sentences.zh: 往年龍舟飄蕩，隔在南岸，聖躬蹈危，臣下破膽，此時宗廟幾至傾覆，為百世之戒。

translations.literal: In past years the dragon boats drifted about, stranded on the southern bank; the Sage Person entered danger, and the ministers below lost their gall—at that time the ancestral temple nearly toppled; let it be a warning for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: In past years your dragon boats were tossed about and stranded on the southern bank; Your Majesty himself faced danger and your ministers were terrified—at that point the ancestral temple nearly fell, and this should stand as a warning for a hundred generations.

sentences.zh: 今又勞兵襲遠，日費千金，中國虛耗，令黠虜玩威，臣竊以為不可。

translations.literal: Now again to weary troops in a distant raid, spending a thousand gold each day, draining central China, letting cunning barbarians make sport of our might—I your servant privately deem this impossible.
translations.idiomatic: Now you would weary the army with another distant strike, spending a thousand gold each day, draining the heartland, and giving cunning barbarians reason to scorn our strength. I respectfully submit that this must not be done.

sentences.zh: 」帝怒，左遷勳為治書執法。

translations.literal: " The Emperor was angry and demoted Xun to Director of Documents and Law Enforcement.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was angered and demoted Xun to Director of Documents and Law Enforcement.

sentences.zh: 勳，信之子也。

translations.literal: Xun was the son of Bao Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was the son of Bao Xin.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，戊申，帝如譙。

translations.literal: Summer, fifth month, on the day Wushen, the Emperor went to Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, during the fifth month, on the day Wushen, the Emperor went to Qiao.

sentences.zh: 5吳丞相北海孫劭卒。

translations.literal: 5. Wu's Chancellor Sun Shao of Beihai died.
translations.idiomatic: 5. Sun Shao of Beihai, chancellor of Wu, died.

sentences.zh: 初，吳當置丞相，眾議歸張昭，吳王曰：「方今多事，職大事責重，非所以優之也。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Wu was about to appoint a chancellor, public opinion settled on Zhang Zhao; the King of Wu said: "At present there are many affairs; the post is large and the responsibility heavy—not the way to treat him with favor.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Wu was about to appoint a chancellor, opinion settled on Zhang Zhao. The King of Wu said, "These are turbulent times; the post is weighty and the responsibility great—not a favor to confer.

sentences.zh: 」及劭卒，百僚復舉昭，吳王曰：「孤豈為子布有愛乎！

translations.literal: " When Shao died, the hundred officials again recommended Zhao; the King of Wu said: "Do I show partial love for Zibu!
translations.idiomatic: When Shao died, the officials again recommended Zhao. The King of Wu said, "Do you think I favor Zibu out of personal affection?

sentences.zh: 領丞相事煩，而此公性剛，所言不從，怨咎將興，非所以益之也。

translations.literal: The duties of handling chancellor's affairs are bothersome, and this lord's nature is hard; when his words are not followed, resentment and blame will arise—not the way to benefit him.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor's duties are onerous, and this man is stiff by nature; when his counsel is ignored, resentment will follow—that is no benefit to him.

sentences.zh: 」六月，以太常顧雍為丞相、平尚書事。

translations.literal: " In the sixth month, Grand Master of Ceremonies Gu Yong was made Chancellor and Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he appointed Gu Yong, Grand Master of Ceremonies, chancellor and director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 雍為人寡言，舉動時當，吳王嘗嘆曰：「顧君不言，言必有中。

translations.literal: Yong was a man of few words; his conduct was always timely. The King of Wu once sighed and said: "Master Gu does not speak—but when he speaks, he surely hits the mark.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was a man of few words whose conduct was always measured. The King of Wu once remarked, "Master Gu rarely speaks, but when he does, he always hits the mark.

sentences.zh: 」至飲宴歡樂之際，左右恐有酒失，而雍必見之，是以不敢肆情。

translations.literal: " At banquets and times of merriment, those at his side feared lapses with wine—but Yong was sure to see them, and so they did not dare indulge freely.
translations.idiomatic: At banquets and moments of merriment, his attendants feared drunken lapses—but Yong was sure to observe them, so they never dared let themselves go.

sentences.zh: 吳王亦曰：「顧公在座，使人不樂。

translations.literal: The King of Wu also said: "When Master Gu is seated, he makes men not merry.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Wu also said, "When Master Gu is present, no one can truly enjoy himself.

sentences.zh: 」其見憚如此。

translations.literal: " Such was the awe in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the awe in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 初領尚書令，封陽遂鄉侯；

translations.literal: When he first took charge as Director of the Masters of Writing, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yangsui township;
translations.idiomatic: When he first served as Director of the Masters of Writing, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yangsui township;

sentences.zh: 拜侯還寺，而家人不知，後聞，乃驚。

translations.literal: returning from receiving the marquisate to his office, his household knew nothing; only when they later heard did they startle.
translations.idiomatic: after receiving his marquisate he returned to his office without telling his family; when they heard of it later, they were astonished.

sentences.zh: 及為相，其所選用文武將吏，各隨能所任，心無適莫。

translations.literal: When he became chancellor, those civilian and military officers he selected and employed he assigned each according to ability; in his heart there was no partiality.
translations.idiomatic: As chancellor, he appointed civil and military officers according to their abilities, without partiality in his heart.

sentences.zh: 時訪逮民間及政職所宜，輒密以聞。

translations.literal: At times he inquired into matters among the people and what governmental duties required, and promptly reported them in secret.
translations.idiomatic: He often inquired into conditions among the people and into what government required, and reported them to the king in confidence.

sentences.zh: 若見納用，則歸之於上；

translations.literal: If his counsel was accepted and employed, he attributed it to the sovereign above;
translations.idiomatic: If his counsel was accepted, he attributed the credit to the king;

sentences.zh: 不用，終不宣洩。

translations.literal: if not accepted, he never disclosed it in the end.
translations.idiomatic: if it was rejected, he never disclosed it.

sentences.zh: 吳王以此重之。

translations.literal: The King of Wu for this reason valued him highly.
translations.idiomatic: For this the King of Wu held him in deep esteem.

sentences.zh: 然於公朝有所陳及，辭色雖順而所執者正；

translations.literal: Yet in open court when he made statements, though his tone and expression were mild, what he held to was upright;
translations.idiomatic: In open court, though his manner was mild, what he upheld was firm;

sentences.zh: 軍國得失，自非面見，口未嘗言。

translations.literal: gain and loss in military and state affairs—unless face to face, his mouth never spoke of them.
translations.idiomatic: as for gains and losses in military and state affairs, unless face to face he never spoke of them.

sentences.zh: 王常令中書郎詣雍有所咨訪，若合雍意，事可施行，即相與反覆究而論之，為設酒食；

translations.literal: The King often sent a Secretariat Gentleman to Yong for consultation; if it accorded with Yong's intent and the matter could be put into practice, they would together go back and forth examining and discussing it, and wine and food would be set out;
translations.idiomatic: The king often sent a secretariat gentleman to consult Yong; if the matter accorded with Yong's judgment and could be implemented, they would discuss it back and forth at length and wine and food would be set out;

sentences.zh: 如不合意，雍即正色改容，默默不言，無所施設。

translations.literal: if it did not accord with his intent, Yong at once composed his expression and changed his countenance, silently saying nothing, setting out nothing.
translations.idiomatic: if it did not accord with his intent, Yong would compose his face, fall silent, and offer nothing further.

sentences.zh: 郎退告王，王曰：「顧公歡悅，是事合宜也；

translations.literal: The Gentleman withdrew and told the King; the King said: "Master Gu is pleased and happy—this matter suits well;
translations.idiomatic: When the gentleman withdrew and reported to the king, the king said, "Master Gu is pleased—that means the matter is suitable;

sentences.zh: 其不言者，是事未平也。

translations.literal: when he does not speak, the matter is not yet settled.
translations.idiomatic: when he does not speak, the matter is not yet settled.

sentences.zh: 孤當重思之。

translations.literal: I must think on it again.
translations.idiomatic: I must reconsider it.

sentences.zh: 」江邊諸將，各欲立功自效，多陳便宜，有所掩襲。

translations.literal: " The various generals along the river each wished to establish merit and prove themselves; many proposed expedient plans for surprise raids.
translations.idiomatic: The generals along the river each wished to prove their merit and often proposed expedient plans for surprise attacks.

sentences.zh: 王以訪雍。

translations.literal: The King consulted Yong about this.
translations.idiomatic: The king consulted Yong about these proposals.

sentences.zh: 雍曰：「臣聞兵法戒於小利，此等所陳，欲邀功名而為其身，非為國也。

translations.literal: Yong said: "Your servant has heard that the art of war warns against small gains—what these men propose is to seize reputation for themselves, not for the state.
translations.idiomatic: Yong said, "The art of war warns against grasping at small gains. These proposals aim at personal glory, not the good of the state.

sentences.zh: 陛下宜禁制，苟不足以曜威損敵，所不宜聽也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty ought to forbid and restrain them; if a plan is not sufficient to display might and harm the enemy, it should not be heard.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should forbid such schemes; if they are not enough to display our might and harm the enemy, they should not be approved.

sentences.zh: 」王從之。

translations.literal: " The King followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The king followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 6利成郡兵蔡方等反，殺太守徐質，推郡人唐咨為主，詔屯騎校尉任福等討平之。

translations.literal: 6. Soldiers of Licheng commandery, Cai Fang and others, rebelled, killed Administrator Xu Zhi, and pushed a man of the commandery Tang Zi as leader; an edict ordered Commandant of the Resolute Cavalry Ren Fu and others to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: 6. Soldiers under Cai Fang and others in Licheng Commandery rebelled, killed the administrator Xu Zhi, and set up a local man, Tang Zi, as their leader; an edict ordered Ren Fu, Commandant of the Resolute Cavalry, and others to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 咨自海道亡入吳，吳人以為將軍。

translations.literal: Zi fled by sea into Wu; Wu made him a General.
translations.idiomatic: Zi fled by sea into Wu, where he was given the rank of general.

sentences.zh: 7秋，七月，立皇子鑒為東武陽王。

translations.literal: 7. Autumn, seventh month, the prince Jian was established as Prince of Dongwuyang.
translations.idiomatic: 7. In the seventh month of autumn, Prince Jian was enfeoffed as Prince of Dongwuyang.

sentences.zh: 8漢諸葛亮至南中，所在戰捷，亮由越巂入，斬雍闓及高定。

translations.literal: 8. Han's Zhuge Liang reached the south; wherever he went he won battles. Liang entered by Yuexi and beheaded Yong Kai and Gao Ding.
translations.idiomatic: 8. Zhuge Liang of Han reached the south, winning wherever he fought. He entered by way of Yuexi and beheaded Yong Kai and Gao Ding.

sentences.zh: 使庲降督益州李恢由益州入，門下督巴西馬忠由牂柯入，擊破諸縣，復與亮合。

translations.literal: He sent Li Hui, Supervisor of Yizhou at Settlement-in-the-South, to enter by Yizhou; Ma Zhong, Supervisor of Baxi in the Palace Secretariat, to enter by Zangge; they defeated various districts and rejoined Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Li Hui, who oversaw Yizhou from Settlement-in-the-South, in from Yizhou, and Ma Zhong, palace gate supervisor of Baxi, in from Zangge; they overran the counties and rejoined Liang.

sentences.zh: 孟獲收闓餘眾以拒亮。

translations.literal: Meng Huo gathered Kai's remaining troops to resist Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Huo gathered Yong Kai's remaining forces to resist Liang.

sentences.zh: 獲素為夷、漢所服，亮募生致之，既得，使觀於營陳之間，問曰：「此軍何如？

translations.literal: Huo was long respected by both Yi and Han. Liang sought to capture him alive; once obtained, he had him observe among the battle formations and asked: "What of this army?
translations.idiomatic: Huo had long commanded respect among both the Yi and the Han. Liang sought to capture him alive; once he had done so, he had Huo observe the army in formation and asked, "What do you make of this army?

sentences.zh: 」獲曰：「向者不知虛實，故敗。

translations.literal: " Huo said: "Before I did not know emptiness and fullness, and so I was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Huo said, "Before I did not know your strength and so I was defeated.

sentences.zh: 今蒙賜觀營陳，若只如此，即定易勝耳。

translations.literal: Now, favored to observe the formations, if it is only like this, I could surely defeat you easily.
translations.idiomatic: Now that I have been allowed to see your formations, if your army is no more than this, I could surely win with ease.

sentences.zh: 」亮笑，縱使更戰。

translations.literal: " Liang smiled and released him to fight again.
translations.idiomatic: Liang smiled and released him to fight again.

sentences.zh: 七縱七擒而亮猶遣獲，獲止不去，曰：「公，天威也，南人不復反矣！

translations.literal: Seven times he released and seven times captured him, yet Liang still sent Huo away; Huo stopped and would not leave, saying: "My lord, this is Heaven's majesty—the southerners will rebel no more!
translations.idiomatic: Seven times Liang released him and seven times he captured him; when Liang released him again, Huo would not go, saying, "My lord, this is the majesty of Heaven—the people of the south will rebel no more!

sentences.zh: 」亮遂至滇池。

translations.literal: " Liang thereupon reached Dian Lake.
translations.idiomatic: Liang then advanced to Dian Lake.

sentences.zh: 益州、永昌、牂柯、越巂四郡皆平，亮即其渠率而用之。

translations.literal: The four commanderies Yizhou, Yongchang, Zangge, and Yuexi were all pacified; Liang at once employed their tribal leaders.
translations.idiomatic: The four commanderies of Yizhou, Yongchang, Zangge, and Yuexi were all pacified, and Liang put their tribal leaders directly to use.

sentences.zh: 或以諫亮，亮曰：「若留外人，則當留兵，兵留則無所食，一不易也；

translations.literal: Some remonstrated with Liang; Liang said: "If we leave outsiders, we must leave troops; if troops remain, there will be no food—first difficulty;
translations.idiomatic: Some remonstrated with Liang. He said, "If we leave outsiders in charge, we must leave troops as well; if troops remain, there will be nothing for them to eat—that is the first difficulty;

sentences.zh: 加夷新傷破，父兄死喪，留外人而無兵者，必成禍患，二不易也；

translations.literal: moreover the Yi have newly been wounded and broken; fathers and elder brothers dead in mourning—if outsiders remain without troops, calamity is sure to arise; second difficulty;
translations.idiomatic: moreover, the Yi have just been defeated and are mourning fathers and elder brothers; if outsiders remain among them without troops, disaster will surely follow—that is the second difficulty;

sentences.zh: 又，夷累有廢殺之罪，自嫌釁重，若留外人，終不相信，三不易也。

translations.literal: again, the Yi repeatedly bear the crime of deposing and killing; they themselves feel the stain is heavy—if outsiders remain, in the end they will not be trusted; third difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: again, the Yi have repeatedly committed treason and regicide and feel their guilt keenly; if outsiders remain, they will never be trusted—that is the third difficulty.

sentences.zh: 今吾欲使不留兵，不運糧，而綱紀粗定，夷、漢粗安故耳。

translations.literal: Now I wish not to leave troops, not to transport grain, yet have rules and discipline roughly settled and Yi and Han roughly secure—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: What I want is to leave no troops and transport no grain, yet still establish order roughly and bring Yi and Han into rough peace—that is all.

sentences.zh: 」亮於是悉收其俊傑孟獲等以為官屬，出其金、銀、丹、漆、耕牛、戰馬以給軍國之用。

translations.literal: " Liang thereupon collected all their outstanding men, Meng Huo and others, to serve as his officers, and brought out their gold, silver, cinnabar, lacquer, plow oxen, and war horses to supply military and state needs.
translations.idiomatic: Liang then took all their leading men, including Meng Huo, into his service as officials, and drew on their gold, silver, cinnabar, lacquer, plow oxen, and war horses to supply the army and the state.

sentences.zh: 自是終亮之世，夷不復反。

translations.literal: From this until the end of Liang's life, the Yi rebelled no more.
translations.idiomatic: From then until the end of Liang's life, the Yi rebelled no more.

sentences.zh: 9八月，帝以舟師自譙循渦入淮。

translations.literal: 9. Eighth month, the Emperor with a naval force went from Qiao along the Wo into the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: 9. In the eighth month, the Emperor led a naval force from Qiao along the Wo River into the Huai.

sentences.zh: 尚書蔣濟表言水道難通，帝不從。

translations.literal: Director of the Masters of Writing Jiang Ji submitted a memorial saying the waterways were hard to pass; the Emperor did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Ji, Director of the Masters of Writing, submitted a memorial stating that the waterways were difficult to navigate, but the Emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，如廣陵故城，臨江觀兵，戎卒十餘萬，旌旗數百里，有渡江之志。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, he went to the old city of Guangling, viewed the troops by the river—more than a hundred thousand soldiers, banners and flags for several hundred li—with intent to cross the river.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter he went to the old city of Guangling and reviewed the troops by the river—more than a hundred thousand soldiers with banners and flags stretching for hundreds of li—with the intention of crossing the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 吳人嚴兵固守。

translations.literal: The men of Wu marshaled troops and held firm.
translations.idiomatic: The men of Wu massed their troops and held firm.

sentences.zh: 時大寒，冰，舟不得入江。

translations.literal: It was bitterly cold at the time; ice formed; boats could not enter the river.
translations.idiomatic: The weather was bitterly cold; ice formed, and the boats could not enter the river.

sentences.zh: 帝見波濤洶湧，嘆曰：「嗟乎，固天所以限南北也！

translations.literal: The Emperor saw the surging waves and sighed, saying: "Alas—surely this is Heaven's means of dividing north and south!
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor saw the surging waves and sighed, "Alas! Surely Heaven itself has set this boundary between north and south!

sentences.zh: 」遂歸。

translations.literal: " He then returned.
translations.idiomatic: He then turned back.

sentences.zh: 孫韶遣將高壽等率敢死之士五百人，於徑路夜要帝，帝大驚。

translations.literal: Sun Shao sent the general Gao Shou and others leading five hundred dare-to-die men, by a bypath at night to intercept the Emperor; the Emperor was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Shao sent the general Gao Shou and others with five hundred dare-to-die soldiers to ambush the Emperor by a back path at night, greatly startling him.

sentences.zh: 壽等獲副車、羽蓋以還。

translations.literal: Shou and the others captured the secondary chariot and feather canopy and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Shou and his men captured the emperor's secondary chariot and imperial canopy and returned.

sentences.zh: 於是戰船數千皆滯不得行，議者欲就留兵屯田，蔣濟以為：「東近湖，北臨淮，若水盛時，賊易為寇，不可安屯。

translations.literal: Thereupon several thousand warships all were stalled and could not proceed; those in council wished to leave troops there for garrison farming; Jiang Ji was of the opinion: "To the east is near a lake, to the north faces the Huai—when water is high, the enemy can easily raid; one cannot safely garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Thousands of warships were now stranded and could not proceed, and some proposed leaving troops behind to farm the land. Jiang Ji argued, "The east lies near a lake and the north faces the Huai; when the waters rise, the enemy can raid with ease—this is no place to establish a garrison.

sentences.zh: 」帝從之，車駕即發。

translations.literal: " The Emperor followed this; the imperial chariot set out at once.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor agreed, and the imperial procession set out at once.

sentences.zh: 還，到精湖，水稍盡，盡留船付濟。

translations.literal: On the return, reaching Jing Lake, the water had somewhat receded; he left all the boats entirely with Ji.
translations.idiomatic: On the return journey, when they reached Jing Lake the waters had receded somewhat, and the Emperor entrusted all the boats to Ji.

sentences.zh: 船連延在數百里中，濟更鑿地作四五道，蹴船令聚；

translations.literal: The ships extended in a line for several hundred li; Ji further dug the ground to make four or five channels and drove the boats to gather them together;
translations.idiomatic: The ships stretched in a line for hundreds of li. Jiang Ji dug four or five channels in the ground and drove the boats to collect them together.

sentences.zh: 豫作土豚遏斷湖水，皆引後船，一時開遏入淮中，乃得還。

translations.literal: He beforehand made earthen dams to block the lake water, drew in all the rear boats, and at one stroke opened the dams to enter the Huai—only then could they return.
translations.idiomatic: He prepared earthen dams to hold back the lake water, drew in all the rear boats, then opened the dams at once and sent them into the Huai River, and so managed to get them back.

sentences.zh: 10十一月，東武陽王鑒薨。

translations.literal: 10. In the eleventh month, the Prince of Dongwuyang, Jian, died.
translations.idiomatic: 10. In the eleventh month, the Prince of Dongwuyang, Jian, died.

sentences.zh: 11十二月，吳番陽賊彭綺攻沒郡縣，眾數萬人。

translations.literal: 11. In the twelfth month, the Fan Yang bandit Peng Qi of Wu attacked and seized commanderies and counties; his forces numbered tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: 11. In the twelfth month, the Fan Yang bandit Peng Qi of Wu attacked and overran commanderies and counties, his forces numbering tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 1春，正月，壬子，帝還洛陽，謂蔣濟曰：「事不可不曉。

translations.literal: 1. Spring, first month, on the day Renzi, the Emperor returned to Luoyang and said to Jiang Ji: "Matters cannot go unexplained.
translations.idiomatic: 1. In spring, the first month, on the day Renzi, the Emperor returned to Luoyang and said to Jiang Ji, "These matters cannot go unexplained.

sentences.zh: 吾前決謂分半燒船於山陽湖中，卿於後致之，略與吾俱至譙。

translations.literal: I had earlier decided that half the boats should be burned in Shanyang Lake; you carried that out afterward, roughly reaching Qiao together with me.
translations.idiomatic: I had decided earlier to burn half the boats in Shanyang Lake; you carried that out afterward, and we reached Qiao at roughly the same time.

sentences.zh: 又每得所陳，實入吾意。

translations.literal: Moreover, each time you presented your views, they truly entered my intent.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, every view you presented truly matched my own thinking.

sentences.zh: 自今討賊計畫，善思論之。

translations.literal: From now on, in plans to attack the rebels, think them through well and discuss them.
translations.idiomatic: From now on, in our plans against the rebels, think them through carefully and discuss them with me.

sentences.zh: 2漢丞相亮欲出軍漢中，前將軍李嚴當知後事，移屯江州，留護軍陳到駐永安，而統屬於嚴。

translations.literal: 2. The Han Chancellor Zhuge Liang planned to march from Hanzhong; the Forward General Li Yan was to manage affairs in the rear, shifted his encampment to Jiangzhou, left Protector-General Chen Dao stationed at Yong'an, under Yan's overall command.
translations.idiomatic: 2. Han Chancellor Zhuge Liang planned to lead an army out from Hanzhong. Forward General Li Yan was to manage affairs in the rear; he moved his camp to Jiangzhou, left Protector-General Chen Dao stationed at Yong'an, and placed him under Yan's overall command.

sentences.zh: 3吳陸遜以所在少穀，表令諸將增廣農畝。

translations.literal: 3. Lu Xun of Wu, because grain was scarce in his region, memorialized that the generals should expand cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: 3. Lu Xun of Wu, finding grain scarce in his region, memorialized that the generals should expand their fields.

sentences.zh: 吳王報曰：「甚善！

translations.literal: The King of Wu replied: "Excellent!
translations.idiomatic: The King of Wu replied, "Excellent!

sentences.zh: 令孤父子親受田，車中八牛，以為四耦，雖未及古人，亦欲與眾均等其勞也。

translations.literal: I shall have myself and my sons personally take up fields—eight oxen in one cart, making four pairs; though not reaching the ancients, I also wish to share labor equally with the masses.
translations.idiomatic: I shall have my sons and me personally work the fields—eight oxen to a cart, making four pairs. Though we fall short of the ancients, I too wish to share the labor equally with everyone else.

sentences.zh: 4帝之為太子也，郭夫人弟有罪，魏郡西部都尉鮑勳治之；

translations.literal: 4. When the Emperor was crown prince, the younger brother of Lady Guo committed a crime; Bao Xun, Western Commandant of Weijun, tried him;
translations.idiomatic: 4. When the Emperor was crown prince, the younger brother of Lady Guo committed a crime, and Bao Xun, Western Commandant of Weijun, prosecuted him.

sentences.zh: 太子請，不能得，由是恨勳。

translations.literal: The crown prince pleaded on his behalf but could not obtain release, and from this bore hatred for Xun.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince pleaded for him but could not win his release, and from that time bore a grudge against Xun.

sentences.zh: 及即位，勳數直諫，帝益忿之。

translations.literal: When he ascended the throne, Xun repeatedly remonstrated frankly, and the Emperor grew ever more resentful.
translations.idiomatic: After he took the throne, Xun repeatedly remonstrated with blunt honesty, and the Emperor grew ever angrier with him.

sentences.zh: 帝伐吳還，屯陳留界。

translations.literal: When the Emperor returned from attacking Wu, he encamped on the border of Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor returned from his campaign against Wu, he encamped on the border of Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 勳為治書執法，太守孫邕見出，過勳。

translations.literal: Xun was Director of Documents and Law Enforcement; the Administrator Sun Yong went out to meet him and passed by Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was Director of Documents and Law Enforcement. Administrator Sun Yong went out to meet him and passed by Xun's position.

sentences.zh: 時營壘未成，但立標埒，邕邪行，不從正道，軍營令史劉曜欲推之，勳以塹壘未成，解止不舉。

translations.literal: At the time the camp fortifications were not complete—only marker lines had been set. Yong walked obliquely, not taking the proper path. Liu Yao, a clerical officer of the garrison, wished to report him, but Xun, because the moat and ramparts were not finished, intervened and halted the report.
translations.idiomatic: The camp fortifications were not yet complete—only marker lines had been laid out. Yong walked at an angle and did not follow the proper path. Liu Yao, a clerical officer of the garrison, wanted to report him, but Xun, because the moat and ramparts were unfinished, intervened and stopped the report.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，詔曰：「勳指鹿作馬，收付廷尉。

translations.literal: The Emperor heard of this and issued an edict: "Xun calls a deer a horse—arrest him and deliver him to the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor heard of this, he issued an edict: "Xun calls a deer a horse—take him and deliver him to the Court of Justice.

sentences.zh: 」廷尉法議，「正刑五歲」，三官駁，「依律，罰金二斤」，帝大怒曰：「勳無活分，而汝等欲縱之！

translations.literal: " The Court of Justice deliberated on the law and proposed "formal punishment of five years." The Three Chief Officials rebutted: "According to the statutes, a fine of two jin." The Emperor was greatly angered and said: "Xun has no portion of life left, yet you wish to release him!
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Justice deliberated on the law and proposed formal punishment of five years. The Three Chief Officials rebutted that, according to statute, the penalty should be a fine of two jin. The Emperor was furious and said, "Xun deserves no chance to live, yet you wish to set him free!

sentences.zh: 收三官已下付刺奸，當令十鼠同穴！

translations.literal: Arrest everyone from the Three Chief Officials downward and deliver them to the Investigators of Impropriety—I shall make ten mice share one hole!
translations.idiomatic: Arrest everyone from the Three Chief Officials on down and hand them over to the Investigators of Impropriety—I shall make ten mice share one hole!

sentences.zh: 」鐘繇、華歆、陳群、辛毗、高柔、衛臻等並表勳父信有功於太祖，求請勳罪，帝不許。

translations.literal: " Zhong Yao, Hua Xin, Chen Qun, Xin Pi, Gao Rou, Wei Zhen, and others jointly memorialized that Xun's father Bao Xin had rendered meritorious service to Emperor Taizu and begged forgiveness for Xun's crime, but the Emperor would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yao, Hua Xin, Chen Qun, Xin Pi, Gao Rou, Wei Zhen, and others jointly memorialized that Xun's father Bao Xin had rendered meritorious service to Emperor Taizu and begged that Xun's crime be forgiven, but the Emperor would not agree.

sentences.zh: 高柔固執不從詔命，帝怒甚，召柔詣臺，遣使者承指至廷尉誅勳。

translations.literal: Gao Rou stubbornly refused to obey the edict. The Emperor was exceedingly angry, summoned Rou to the palace, and sent an envoy bearing his instruction to the Court of Justice to execute Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Rou stubbornly refused to obey the edict. The Emperor was furious, summoned Rou to the palace, and sent an envoy bearing his direct order to the Court of Justice to execute Xun.

sentences.zh: 勳死，乃遣柔還寺。

translations.literal: After Xun died, he sent Rou back to his office.
translations.idiomatic: After Xun was executed, the Emperor sent Rou back to his office.

sentences.zh: 驃騎將軍都陽侯曹洪，家富而性吝嗇，帝在東宮，嘗從洪貸絹百匹，不稱意，恨之。

translations.literal: General of Flying Cavalry and Marquis of Duyang Cao Hong was wealthy but stingy by nature. When the Emperor was in the Eastern Palace, he once borrowed a hundred bolts of silk from Hong but was not satisfied, and bore resentment.
translations.idiomatic: General of Flying Cavalry and Marquis of Duyang Cao Hong was wealthy but miserly by nature. When the Emperor was in the Eastern Palace, he once borrowed a hundred bolts of silk from Hong and was displeased with what he received, and bore a grudge because of it.

sentences.zh: 遂以捨客犯法，下獄當死，群臣並救，莫能得。

translations.literal: Thereupon, on the charge that a resident retainer had violated the law, Hong was imprisoned and sentenced to death; all the ministers together pleaded for him, but none could succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon, on the charge that a resident retainer had broken the law, Hong was thrown into prison and sentenced to death. All the ministers pleaded for him together, but none could save him.

sentences.zh: 卞太后責怒帝曰：「梁、沛之間，非子廉無有今日！

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Bian scolded the Emperor in anger: "Between Liang and Pei, without Zilian there would be no today of yours!
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Bian scolded the Emperor in anger, "Between Liang and Pei, without Zilian you would not have what you have today!

sentences.zh: 」又謂郭后曰：「令曹洪今日死，吾明日敕帝廢後矣！

translations.literal: " She also said to Empress Guo: "If Cao Hong dies today, tomorrow I shall command the Emperor to depose the empress!
translations.idiomatic: She also said to Empress Guo, "If Cao Hong dies today, tomorrow I shall command the Emperor to depose you as empress!

sentences.zh: 」於是郭后泣涕屢請，乃得免官，削爵土。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Empress Guo wept and repeatedly pleaded, and Hong was spared death—only stripped of office and reduced in rank and fief.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Empress Guo wept and repeatedly pleaded on his behalf, and Hong was spared death but stripped of office and reduced in rank and fief.

sentences.zh: 5初，郭后無子，帝使母養平原王叡；

translations.literal: 5. At the beginning, Empress Guo had no son; the Emperor had her raise the Prince of Pingyuan, Rui.
translations.idiomatic: 5. At the beginning, Empress Guo had no son, so the Emperor had her raise the Prince of Pingyuan, Rui.

sentences.zh: 以叡母甄夫人被誅，故未建為嗣。

translations.literal: Because Rui's mother, Lady Zhen, had been executed, he had not yet been established as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Because Rui's mother, Lady Zhen, had been executed, he had not yet been established as heir.

sentences.zh: 叡事後甚謹，後亦愛之。

translations.literal: Rui served the empress with great care, and she also loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Rui served the empress with great care, and she came to love him as well.

sentences.zh: 帝與叡獵，見子母鹿，帝親射殺其母，命叡射其子。

translations.literal: The Emperor went hunting with Rui and saw a doe and fawn; the Emperor personally shot and killed the mother and ordered Rui to shoot the fawn.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor went hunting with Rui and saw a doe and fawn. The Emperor personally shot and killed the mother, then ordered Rui to shoot the fawn.

sentences.zh: 叡泣曰：「陛下已殺其母，臣不忍復殺其子。

translations.literal: Rui wept and said: "Your Majesty has already killed its mother; your servant cannot bear to kill its child as well.
translations.idiomatic: Rui wept and said, "Your Majesty has already killed its mother. I cannot bear to kill its child as well.

sentences.zh: 」帝即放弓矢，為之惻然。

translations.literal: " The Emperor at once lowered bow and arrow, moved to compassion.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor at once lowered his bow and arrows, moved to compassion.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，帝疾篤，乃立叡為太子。

translations.literal: Summer, fifth month: the Emperor's illness grew grave, and he established Rui as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fifth month, the Emperor's illness grew grave, and he established Rui as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，召中軍大將軍曹真、鎮軍大將軍陳群、撫軍大將軍司馬懿，並受遺詔輔政。

translations.literal: On Bingchen, he summoned the Grand General of the Central Army Cao Zhen, the Grand General Who Stabilizes the Army Chen Qun, and the Grand General Who Pacifies the Army Sima Yi, all receiving the testamentary edict to assist in government.
translations.idiomatic: On Bingchen he summoned Grand General of the Central Army Cao Zhen, Grand General Who Stabilizes the Army Chen Qun, and Grand General Who Pacifies the Army Sima Yi, all to receive the testamentary edict and assist in government.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，帝殂。

translations.literal: On Dingsi, the Emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: On Dingsi, the Emperor died.

sentences.zh: ::陳壽評曰：文帝天資文藻，下筆成章，博聞強識，才藝兼該。

translations.literal: Chen Shou's evaluation: Emperor Wen was gifted by nature with literary refinement, could compose essays at a stroke, was widely learned with a strong memory, and combined many talents and arts.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shou remarked: Emperor Wen was gifted by nature with literary refinement, could compose essays at a stroke, was widely learned with a strong memory, and united many talents and arts.

sentences.zh: 若加之曠大之度，勵以公平之誠，邁志存道，克廣德心，則古之賢主，何遠之有哉！

translations.literal: If one added to this a broad and magnanimous measure, encouraged by fairness and sincerity, advancing his will to embrace the Way and fully extending the heart of virtue, then how far would the sage rulers of antiquity be!
translations.idiomatic: If to this one added a broad and magnanimous spirit, encouraged by fairness and sincerity, advancing his will to embrace the Way and fully extending the heart of virtue, then how far would the sage rulers of antiquity be!

sentences.zh: 6太子即皇帝位，尊皇太后曰太皇太后，皇后曰皇太后。

translations.literal: 6. The crown prince assumed the imperial throne, honoring the Empress Dowager as Grand Empress Dowager and the Empress as Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: 6. The crown prince assumed the imperial throne, honoring the Empress Dowager as Grand Empress Dowager and the Empress as Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 初，明帝在東宮，不交朝臣，不問政事，惟潛思書籍；

translations.literal: At the beginning, when Mingdi was in the Eastern Palace, he did not associate with court ministers or inquire into governance—only pondered books in secret;
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning, when Mingdi was in the Eastern Palace, he did not associate with court ministers or inquire into governance, but only pondered books in secret.

sentences.zh: 即位之後，群下想聞風采。

translations.literal: After he ascended the throne, officials below yearned to witness his bearing.
translations.idiomatic: After he took the throne, officials throughout the court yearned to witness his bearing.

sentences.zh: 居數日，獨見侍中劉曄，語盡日，眾人側聽，曄既出，問：「何如？

translations.literal: After several days, he alone received Attendant Within Liu Ye and spoke with him the whole day. The crowd listened from the side. When Ye came out, they asked: "How was it?
translations.idiomatic: After several days, he received Attendant Within Liu Ye alone and spoke with him the whole day. The others listened from the side. When Ye came out, they asked, "How was he?

sentences.zh: 」曰：「秦始皇、漢孝武之儔，才具微不及耳。

translations.literal: " He said: "A match for Qin Shihuang and Emperor Xiaowu of Han—his talent and capacity fall slightly short, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "He is a match for Qin Shihuang and Emperor Xiaowu of Han—his talent and capacity fall only slightly short."

sentences.zh: 」帝初蒞政，陳群上疏曰：「夫臣下雷同，是非相蔽，國之大患也。

translations.literal: " When the Emperor first took up governance, Chen Qun submitted a memorial: "When subordinates echo one another and right and wrong mutually obscure each other, this is a great calamity for the state.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor first took up governance, Chen Qun submitted a memorial: "When subordinates echo one another and right and wrong mutually obscure each other, this is a great calamity for the state.

sentences.zh: 若不和睦則有仇黨，有仇黨則毀譽無端，毀譽無端則真偽失實，此皆不可不深察也。

translations.literal: If there is no harmony, then factional cliques arise; when cliques arise, praise and blame lose proper grounding; when praise and blame lose grounding, truth and falsehood lose their reality—these all must be examined deeply.
translations.idiomatic: If there is no harmony, factional cliques arise; when cliques arise, praise and blame lose proper grounding; when praise and blame lose grounding, truth and falsehood lose their reality—all of this must be examined deeply.

sentences.zh: 7癸未<ref>癸未是年五月辛丑朔，無癸未，疑為六月事。

translations.literal: 7. On the day Guiwei<ref>On Guiwei: that year's fifth month had Xinchou as new moon—there was no day Guiwei; this is suspected to belong to the sixth month.
translations.idiomatic: 7. On the day Guiwei—note: that year's fifth month had Xinchou as new moon, so there was no day Guiwei; this is suspected to refer to the sixth month.

sentences.zh: 六月庚午朔，為十四日。

translations.literal: The sixth month's new moon on Gengwu would be the fourteenth day.
translations.idiomatic: Taking the sixth month's new moon on Gengwu, that would be the fourteenth day.

sentences.zh: </ref>，追謚甄夫人曰文昭皇后。

translations.literal: </ref>, the posthumous title Wen Zhao Empress was conferred upon Lady Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: The posthumous title Wen Zhao Empress was conferred upon Lady Zhen.

sentences.zh: 8壬辰<ref>壬辰是年五月辛丑朔，無壬辰，疑為六月事。

translations.literal: 8. On the day Renchen<ref>On Renchen: that year's fifth month had Xinchou as new moon—there was no day Renchen; this is suspected to belong to the sixth month.
translations.idiomatic: 8. On the day Renchen—note: that year's fifth month had Xinchou as new moon, so there was no day Renchen; this is suspected to refer to the sixth month.

sentences.zh: 六月庚午朔，為二十三日。

translations.literal: The sixth month's new moon on Gengwu would be the twenty-third day.
translations.idiomatic: Taking the sixth month's new moon on Gengwu, that would be the twenty-third day.

sentences.zh: </ref>，立皇弟蕤為陽平王。

translations.literal: </ref>, the Emperor's younger brother Rui was established as Prince of Yangping.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's younger brother Rui was established as Prince of Yangping.

sentences.zh: 9六月，戊寅，葬文帝於首陽陵。

translations.literal: 9. In the sixth month, on Wuyin, Emperor Wen was buried at Shouyang Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: 9. In the sixth month, on Wuyin, Emperor Wen was buried at Shouyang Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 10吳王聞魏有大喪，秋，八月，自將攻江夏郡，太守文聘堅守。

translations.literal: 10. When the King of Wu heard that Wei had a great bereavement, in autumn, the eighth month, he personally led an attack on Jiangxia Commandery; the Administrator Wen Pin held firm in defense.
translations.idiomatic: 10. When the King of Wu heard that Wei had suffered a great bereavement, in autumn, the eighth month, he personally led an attack on Jiangxia Commandery, but Administrator Wen Pin held firm in defense.

sentences.zh: 朝議欲發兵救之。

translations.literal: At court they debated sending troops to rescue it.
translations.idiomatic: At court they debated sending troops to rescue the city.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「權習水戰，所以敢下船陸攻者，冀掩不備也。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Quan is skilled in naval warfare—he dare come ashore to attack only because he hopes to catch us unprepared.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Quan is skilled in naval warfare. He dares come ashore to attack only because he hopes to catch us unprepared.

sentences.zh: 今已與聘相拒。

translations.literal: Now he is already locked in opposition with Pin.
translations.idiomatic: Now he is already locked in opposition with Pin.

sentences.zh: 夫攻守勢倍，終不敢久也。

translations.literal: In attack and defense the defender holds double the advantage—he will not dare remain long in the end.
translations.idiomatic: In attack and defense the defender holds double the advantage, and in the end he will not dare remain long.

sentences.zh: 」先是，朝廷遣治書侍御史荀禹慰勞邊方，禹到江夏，發所經縣兵及所從步騎千人乘山舉火，吳王遁走。

translations.literal: " Earlier, the court had sent Supervising Imperial Secretary Xun Yu to comfort the frontier. When Yu reached Jiangxia, he mobilized the county troops along his route and the thousand foot and cavalry he brought, lit beacon fires on the hills, and the King of Wu fled.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the court had sent Supervising Imperial Secretary Xun Yu to comfort the frontier regions. When Yu reached Jiangxia, he mobilized the county troops along his route and the thousand foot and cavalry he had brought, lit beacon fires on the hills, and the King of Wu fled.

sentences.zh: 11辛巳，立皇子冏為清河王。

translations.literal: 11. On Xinsi, the Prince Jiong was established as Prince of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: 11. On Xinsi, Prince Jiong was established as Prince of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 12吳左將軍諸葛瑾等寇襄陽，司馬懿擊破之，斬其部將張霸。

translations.literal: 12. Zuo General Zhuge Jin of Wu and others raided Xiangyang; Sima Yi defeated them and beheaded their subordinate general Zhang Ba.
translations.idiomatic: 12. Wu's Left General Zhuge Jin and others raided Xiangyang. Sima Yi defeated them and beheaded their subordinate general Zhang Ba.

sentences.zh: 曹真又破其別將於尋陽。

translations.literal: Cao Zhen also defeated their detached commander at Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Zhen also defeated their detached commander at Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 13吳丹陽、吳、會山民復為寇，攻沒屬縣。

translations.literal: 13. Mountain people of Danyang, Wu, and Kuai in Wu again became bandits, attacking and seizing subordinate counties.
translations.idiomatic: 13. Mountain people of Danyang, Wu, and Kuai in Wu again became bandits, attacking and overran subordinate counties.

sentences.zh: 吳王分三郡險地為東安郡，以綏南將軍全琮領太守。

translations.literal: The King of Wu partitioned dangerous territory from three commanderies to form Dong'an Commandery, appointing General Who Pacifies the South Quan Cong as Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Wu carved out dangerous territory from three commanderies to form Dong'an Commandery and appointed General Who Pacifies the South Quan Cong as its administrator.

sentences.zh: 琮至，明賞罰，招誘降附，數年，得萬餘人。

translations.literal: When Cong arrived, he made rewards and punishments clear, invited surrender and gained adherents; within several years he acquired more than ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: When Cong arrived, he made rewards and punishments clear, invited surrender and won adherents, and within several years gathered more than ten thousand people.

sentences.zh: 吳王召琮還牛渚，罷東安郡。

translations.literal: The King of Wu recalled Cong to Niuzhu and abolished Dong'an Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Wu recalled Cong to Niuzhu and abolished Dong'an Commandery.

sentences.zh: 14冬，十月，清河王冏卒。

translations.literal: 14. Winter, tenth month: the Prince of Qinghe, Jiong, died.
translations.idiomatic: 14. In winter, the tenth month, the Prince of Qinghe, Jiong, died.

sentences.zh: 15吳陸遜陳便宜，勸吳王以施德緩刑，寬賦息調。

translations.literal: 15. Lu Xun of Wu presented practical proposals, urging the King of Wu to show virtue, relax punishments, lighten taxes, and reduce levies.
translations.idiomatic: 15. Lu Xun of Wu presented practical proposals, urging the King of Wu to show virtue, relax punishments, lighten taxes, and reduce levies.

sentences.zh: 又云：「忠讜之言，不能極陳；

translations.literal: He also said: "Loyal and forthright words cannot be fully stated;
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Loyal and forthright words cannot be fully stated;

sentences.zh: 求容小臣，數以利聞。

translations.literal: petty ministers seeking favor repeatedly report only what is advantageous."
translations.idiomatic: petty ministers seeking favor repeatedly report only what is advantageous."

sentences.zh: 」王報曰：「《書》載：『予違汝弼』，而雲不敢極陳，何得為忠讜哉！

translations.literal: " The King replied: "The Documents record: 'When I err, you shall assist me'—yet you say you dare not speak fully; how can that be loyal and forthright!
translations.idiomatic: The King replied, "The Documents record, 'When I err, you shall assist me'—yet you say you dare not speak fully. How can that be loyal and forthright!

sentences.zh: 」於是令有司盡寫科條，使郎中褚逢繼以就遜及諸葛瑾，意所不安，令損益之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he ordered the relevant offices to copy out all statutes and ordinances fully, sent Attendant Chu Feng to follow up with Lu Xun and Zhuge Jin, and wherever they felt uneasy, had them revise for increase or decrease.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he ordered the relevant offices to copy out all statutes and ordinances in full, sent Attendant Chu Feng to follow up with Lu Xun and Zhuge Jin, and wherever they felt uneasy, had them revise them for increase or decrease.

sentences.zh: 16十二月，以鍾繇為太傅、曹休為大司馬，都督揚州如故；

translations.literal: 16. In the twelfth month, Zhong Yao was made Grand Tutor; Cao Xiu was made Grand Marshal, continuing to supervise Yang Province as before;
translations.idiomatic: 16. In the twelfth month, Zhong Yao was made Grand Tutor, and Cao Xiu was made Grand Marshal, continuing to supervise Yang Province as before.

sentences.zh: 曹真為大將軍，華歆為太尉，王朗為司徒，陳群為司空，司馬懿為驃騎大將軍。

translations.literal: Cao Zhen was made Grand General; Hua Xin, Grand Commandant; Wang Lang, Minister over the Masses; Chen Qun, Minister of Works; Sima Yi, Grand General of Flying Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Zhen was made Grand General; Hua Xin, Grand Commandant; Wang Lang, Minister over the Masses; Chen Qun, Minister of Works; and Sima Yi, Grand General of Flying Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 歆讓位於管寧，帝不許。

translations.literal: Xin yielded his position to Guan Ning; the Emperor would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Xin offered to yield his position to Guan Ning, but the Emperor would not permit it.

sentences.zh: 徵寧為光祿大夫，敕青州給安車吏從，以禮發遣，寧復不至。

translations.literal: Ning was summoned as Grand Master for Glorious Happiness; Qing Province was ordered to provide a comfort carriage and attendants, dispatched with full ceremony—but Ning again did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Ning was summoned as Grand Master for Glorious Happiness. Qing Province was ordered to provide a comfort carriage and attendants and to dispatch him with full ceremony, but Ning again did not come.

sentences.zh: 17是歲，吳交趾太守士燮卒，吳王以燮子徽為安遠將軍，領九真太守，以校尉陳時代燮。

translations.literal: 17. That year, Shi Xie, Administrator of Jiaozhi in Wu, died. The King of Wu made Xie's son Hui General Who Pacifies the Distance and Administrator of Jiuzhen, appointing Commandant Chen Shi to replace Xie.
translations.idiomatic: 17. That year, Shi Xie, Administrator of Jiaozhi in Wu, died. The King of Wu made Xie's son Hui General Who Pacifies the Distance and Administrator of Jiuzhen, and appointed Commandant Chen Shi to replace Xie.

sentences.zh: 交州刺史呂岱以交趾絕遠，表分海南三郡為交州，以將軍戴良為刺史；

translations.literal: Inspector of Jiaozhi Lü Dai, because Jiaozhi was extremely remote, memorialized to divide the three commanderies south of the sea into Jiaozhi Province, with General Dai Liang as Inspector;
translations.idiomatic: Inspector of Jiaozhi Lü Dai, finding Jiaozhi extremely remote, memorialized to divide the three commanderies south of the sea into Jiaozhi Province, with General Dai Liang as inspector.

sentences.zh: 海東四郡為廣州，岱自為刺史；

translations.literal: the four commanderies east of the sea were made Guang Province, with Dai himself as Inspector;
translations.idiomatic: The four commanderies east of the sea were made Guang Province, with Dai himself as inspector;

sentences.zh: 遣良與時南入。

translations.literal: He sent Liang and Shi south together.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Liang and Shi south together.

sentences.zh: 而徽自署交趾太守，發宗兵拒良，良留合浦。

translations.literal: But Hui styled himself Administrator of Jiaozhi, mobilized clan troops to resist Liang, and Liang halted at Hepu.
translations.idiomatic: But Hui styled himself Administrator of Jiaozhi, mobilized clan troops to resist Liang, and Liang halted at Hepu.

translations.idiomatic: Lin, a clerk Shi Xie had raised up, kowtowed to remonstrate with Hui and urged him to welcome Dai Liang.
