translations.literal: Hui was angry, had Lin flogged to death; Lin's elder brother Zhi led clan troops to attack but failed.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was angry and had Lin flogged to death. Lin's elder brother Zhi rallied clan troops to attack but failed.

sentences.zh: 呂岱上疏請討徽，督兵三千人，晨夜浮海而往。

translations.literal: Lü Dai submitted a memorial requesting to subdue Hui, supervised three thousand troops, and sailed by sea day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Dai submitted a memorial requesting permission to subdue Hui, supervised three thousand troops, and sailed by sea day and night.

sentences.zh: 或謂岱曰：「徽藉累世之恩，為一州所附，未易輕也。

translations.literal: Someone said to Dai: "Hui relies on generations of favor and has the whole province's allegiance—he is not easily taken lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Someone said to Dai, "Hui relies on generations of favor and has the allegiance of the whole province. He is not to be taken lightly.

sentences.zh: 」岱曰：「今徽雖懷逆計，未虞吾之卒至；

translations.literal: " Dai said: "Now although Hui harbors treasonous designs, he does not anticipate our sudden arrival;
translations.idiomatic: Dai said, "Now although Hui harbors treasonous designs, he does not anticipate our sudden arrival.

sentences.zh: 若我潛軍輕舉，掩其無備，破之必也。

translations.literal: If we move troops secretly with a swift strike and catch him unprepared, we shall surely break him.
translations.idiomatic: If we move troops secretly with a swift strike and catch him unprepared, we shall surely defeat him.

sentences.zh: 稽留不速，使得生心，嬰城固守，七郡百蠻雲合響應，雖有智者，誰能圖之！

translations.literal: If we delay and do not go quickly, giving him time to take heart, hold the walls in siege defense, and gather the seven commanderies and hundreds of tribes like clouds answering in unison—even with a wise man, who could overcome that!
translations.idiomatic: If we delay and do not go quickly, giving him time to take heart, hold the walls in siege defense, and gather the seven commanderies and hundreds of tribes like clouds answering in unison—even with a wise man, who could overcome that!

sentences.zh: 」遂行，過合浦，與良俱進。

translations.literal: " He then set out, passed Hepu, and advanced together with Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He then set out, passed Hepu, and advanced together with Liang.

sentences.zh: 岱以燮弟子輔為師友從事，遣往說徽。

translations.literal: Dai appointed Xie's nephew Fu as Gentleman Companion in Friendship and sent him to persuade Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Dai appointed Xie's nephew Fu as Gentleman Companion in Friendship and sent him to persuade Hui.

sentences.zh: 徽率其兄弟六人出降，岱皆斬之。

translations.literal: Hui led his six brothers out to surrender, and Dai beheaded them all.
translations.idiomatic: Hui led his six brothers out to surrender, and Dai beheaded them all.

sentences.zh: ::孫盛論曰：夫柔遠能邇，莫善於信。

translations.literal: Sun Sheng remarked: In winning over the distant and governing those near, nothing is better than trustworthiness.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng wrote: To win over distant peoples and keep those near at peace, nothing serves better than good faith.

sentences.zh: 呂岱師友士輔，使通信誓；

translations.literal: Lü Dai's Gentleman Companion Fu, he had him convey pledges of mutual trust;
translations.idiomatic: Lü Dai sent his Gentleman Companion Fu to exchange pledges of trust;

sentences.zh: 徽兄弟肉袒，推心委命，岱因滅之以要功利，君子是以知呂氏之祚不延者也。

translations.literal: The Hui brothers bared their breasts in submission and entrusted themselves wholeheartedly, yet Dai destroyed them to demand profit and success—hence gentlemen knew the Lü clan's fortune would not endure.
translations.idiomatic: The Hui brothers stripped to the waist and surrendered in full trust, yet Dai destroyed them to seize profit and glory. From this, men of discernment knew the Lü line would not long endure.

sentences.zh: 18徽大將軍甘醴及桓治率吏民共攻岱，岱奮擊，破之。

translations.literal: 18. Hui's Grand General Gan Li and Huan Zhi led officials and people together to attack Dai; Dai fought fiercely and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: 18. Hui's Grand General Gan Li and Huan Zhi rallied officials and commoners to attack Dai, but Dai fought back hard and routed them.

sentences.zh: 於是除廣州，復為交州如故。

translations.literal: Thereupon Guang Province was abolished, and Jiao Province was restored as before.
translations.idiomatic: Guang Province was then abolished, and Jiao Province was restored to its former status.

sentences.zh: 岱進討九真，斬獲以萬數；

translations.literal: Dai advanced to campaign in Jiuzhen, beheading and capturing by the tens of thousands;
translations.idiomatic: Dai pressed into Jiuzhen, killing and capturing enemies by the tens of thousands;

sentences.zh: 又遣從事南宣威命，暨徼外扶南、林邑、堂明諸王，各遣使入貢於吳。

translations.literal: He also sent a staff officer south to proclaim imperial authority, and beyond the frontier the kings of Funan, Linyi, Tangming, and others each sent envoys to Wu to pay tribute.
translations.idiomatic: He also dispatched a staff officer south to proclaim Wu's authority, whereupon the kings beyond the frontier—Funan, Linyi, Tangming, and the rest—each sent envoys to Wu bearing tribute.

sentences.zh: 烈祖明皇帝上之上

translations.literal: The Reign of Emperor Ming the Brilliant Ancestor, Part One (upper)
translations.idiomatic: The Reign of Emperor Ming the Brilliant Ancestor, Part One

sentences.zh: 1春，吳解煩督胡綜、鄱陽太守周魴擊彭綺，生獲之。

translations.literal: 1. In spring, Wu's Colonel Who Relieves Distress Hu Zong and Administrator of Poyang Zhou Fang attacked Peng Qi and captured him alive.
translations.idiomatic: 1. In spring, Wu's Colonel Who Relieves Distress Hu Zong and the Administrator of Poyang, Zhou Fang, attacked Peng Qi and took him alive.

sentences.zh: 初，綺自言舉義兵，為魏討吳，議者以為因此伐吳，必有所克。

translations.literal: Earlier, Qi had declared that he was raising righteous troops to punish Wu on Wei's behalf, and those who deliberated thought that for this reason an attack on Wu would surely succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Qi had proclaimed that he was raising a righteous army to punish Wu on Wei's behalf, and many at court argued that a Wu campaign launched on this pretext was sure to succeed.

sentences.zh: 帝以問中書令太原孫資，資曰：「番陽宗人，前後數有舉義者，眾弱謀淺，旋輒乖散。

translations.literal: The Emperor asked Palace Secretary Sun Zi of Taiyuan about it, and Zi said: "Poyang clansmen have several times before raised righteous armies, but their forces were few, their plans shallow, and they soon fell apart.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked Palace Secretary Sun Zi of Taiyuan for his view. Zi said, "Clansmen from Poyang have raised righteous armies more than once before, but their forces were small, their plans shallow, and they soon scattered.

sentences.zh: 昔文皇帝嘗密論賊形勢，言洞浦殺萬人，得船千數，數日間，船人復會。

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Wen once discussed the enemy's situation in private, saying that at Dongpu ten thousand men were killed and a thousand-odd ships taken, yet within days the ships and men reassembled.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen once discussed the enemy's strength in private, observing that at Dongpu ten thousand men were killed and more than a thousand ships captured, yet within days the ships and crews had gathered again.

sentences.zh: 江陵被圍歷月，權裁以千數百兵住東門，而其土地無崩解者，是有法禁上下相維之明驗也。

translations.literal: When Jiangling was besieged for months, Sun Quan kept only a thousand-odd troops at the east gate, yet his territory did not collapse—clear proof that laws and discipline bind superiors and subordinates together.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangling was besieged for months, Sun Quan kept only a thousand-odd troops at the east gate, yet his domain did not crumble. That was clear proof that strict law and mutual obligation held his realm together.

sentences.zh: 以此推綺，懼未能為權腹心大疾也。

translations.literal: Judging Qi by this standard, I fear he will not become a grave affliction in Sun Quan's innermost counsels.
translations.idiomatic: By that measure, I doubt Qi will ever become a mortal threat at the heart of Sun Quan's power.

sentences.zh: 」至是，綺果敗亡。

translations.literal: " By this time, Qi indeed met defeat and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: " And so it proved: Qi was soon defeated and destroyed.

sentences.zh: 王朗往視園陵，見百姓多貧困，而帝方營修宮室，朗上疏諫曰：「昔大禹欲拯天下之大患，故先卑其宮室，儉其衣食；

translations.literal: Wang Lang went to inspect the park and tombs, saw that the common people were largely impoverished while the Emperor was just then building and repairing palaces, and submitted a memorial remonstrating: "In old times Yu the Great wished to rescue the realm from great calamity, and so first lowered his palaces and made his food and clothing spare;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lang went to inspect the park and tombs. Seeing the people widely impoverished while the Emperor was busy building and repairing palaces, he submitted a memorial of remonstrance: "Long ago, Yu the Great sought to deliver the world from great disaster, and so he first made his halls low and his food and clothing plain;

sentences.zh: 勾踐欲廣其御兒之疆，亦約其身以及家，儉其家以施國；

translations.literal: Gou Jian wished to expand the borders he would bequeath to his son, and so also restrained himself and extended that restraint to his household, making his household frugal to benefit the state;
translations.idiomatic: Gou Jian wished to enlarge the realm he would leave his son, and so he restrained himself, extended that restraint to his household, and made his household's thrift serve the state;

sentences.zh: 漢之文、景欲恢弘祖業，故割意於百金之臺，昭儉於弋綈之服；

translations.literal: Emperors Wen and Jing of Han wished to expand their ancestral enterprise, and so renounced the hundred-gold terrace and displayed frugality in robes of coarse silk;
translations.idiomatic: Emperors Wen and Jing of Han sought to enlarge the work of their forebears, and so they forswore the hundred-gold terrace and wore their thrift plainly in robes of coarse silk;

sentences.zh: 霍去病中才之將，猶以匈奴未滅，不治第宅。

translations.literal: Huo Qubing, a general of middling talent, still because the Xiongnu were not yet destroyed, did not build a mansion.
translations.idiomatic: Even Huo Qubing, a general of only middling gifts, refused to build a mansion while the Xiongnu remained undefeated.

sentences.zh: 明恤遠者略近，事外者簡內也。

translations.literal: The enlightened care for what is distant and set aside what is near; those who attend to external affairs simplify internal ones.
translations.idiomatic: The wise give priority to distant concerns and set aside immediate ones; those who look outward simplify what lies within.

sentences.zh: 今建始之前，足用列朝會；

translations.literal: Today, before Jianshi, there is enough space to hold court assemblies;
translations.idiomatic: As things stand, the halls before Jianshi are ample for holding court;

sentences.zh: 崇華之後，足用序內官；

translations.literal: after Chonghua, enough to arrange the inner palace offices;
translations.idiomatic: the chambers beyond Chonghua are enough to house the inner palace offices;

sentences.zh: 華林、天淵，足用展游宴。

translations.literal: Hualin and Tianyuan are enough to hold excursions and banquets.
translations.idiomatic: Hualin and Tianyuan are enough for excursions and feasts.

sentences.zh: 若且先成象魏，修城池，其餘一切須豐年，專以勤耕農為務，習戎備為事，則民充兵強而寇戎賓服矣。

translations.literal: If for now you first complete the Elephant Gate and repair the city walls, and leave all the rest for years of abundance, devoting yourself solely to diligent farming and making military preparedness your task, then the people will be full and the army strong, and invaders and barbarians will submit as guests.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty would first finish the Elephant Gate and repair the city walls, deferring all other works until years of plenty, and devote yourself to farming and military readiness, then the people will prosper, the army grow strong, and enemies and barbarians alike will submit.

sentences.zh: 臨發，上疏曰：「先帝創業未半，而中道崩殂。

translations.literal: Prior to departure, he submitted a memorial saying: "The late Emperor had not yet finished founding his enterprise when he passed away midway.
translations.idiomatic: Before setting out, he submitted a memorial that began: "The late Emperor had not yet finished founding his enterprise when he died midway.

sentences.zh: 今天下三分，益州疲敝，此誠危急存亡之秋也。

translations.literal: Today the realm is divided in three, and Yizhou is exhausted and depleted—truly this is a season of peril in which survival or destruction hangs in the balance.
translations.idiomatic: Today the realm is divided in three, and Yizhou is worn down and depleted. This is truly the hour when survival or ruin hangs in the balance.

sentences.zh: 然侍衛之臣不懈於內，忠志之士忘身於外者，蓋追先帝之殊遇，欲報之於陛下也。

translations.literal: Yet the ministers who attend Your Majesty never slacken within, and loyal men who forget themselves in service abroad do so because they recall the late Emperor's extraordinary favor and wish to repay it to Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the ministers who attend you never slacken at court, and loyal men who risk themselves abroad do so because they remember the late Emperor's extraordinary kindness and wish to repay it to Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 誠宜開張聖聽，以光先帝遺德，恢弘志士之氣；

translations.literal: It is truly fitting to open wide your sacred hearing, to brighten the late Emperor's legacy, and to expand the spirit of men of resolve;
translations.idiomatic: You should truly open your ears to wise counsel, honor the late Emperor's legacy, and inspire the spirit of loyal men;

sentences.zh: 不宜妄自菲薄，引喻失義，以塞忠諫之路也。

translations.literal: you should not undervalue yourself without cause, nor cite improper comparisons, thereby blocking the path of loyal remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: you should not undervalue yourself without cause or speak in ways that miss the point, for that would shut off the path of loyal remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 「宮中、府中，俱為一體，陟罰臧否，不宜異同。

translations.literal: "Within the palace and within the government, all are one body; in promoting, punishing, praising, or condemning, there should be no difference.
translations.idiomatic: "Palace and government are one body. In reward and punishment, praise and blame, there should be no double standard.

sentences.zh: 若有作奸犯科及為忠善者，宜付有司論其刑賞，以昭陛下平明之理，不宜偏私，使內外異法也。

translations.literal: If there are those who commit wrongdoing and violate the law, or who perform loyal and good deeds, they should be handed to the proper offices to determine punishment and reward, thereby displaying Your Majesty's fair and clear governance; you should not show partiality and make inner and outer realms subject to different laws.
translations.idiomatic: Whether a man commits crime or performs loyal service, he should be judged by the proper offices according to law and merit, so that your fairness may be plain. Do not show favoritism and make one law for the palace and another for the realm.

sentences.zh: 「侍中、侍郎郭攸之、費禕、董允等，此皆良實，志慮忠純，是以先帝簡拔以遺陛下。

translations.literal: "Palace Attendants and Gentlemen-in-Attendance Guo Youzhi, Fei Yi, Dong Yun, and the like—all are honest and reliable, their intent loyal and pure; therefore the late Emperor selected and left them to Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: "Palace Attendants Guo Youzhi, Fei Yi, Dong Yun, and the like are honest and trustworthy, loyal and pure in purpose. The late Emperor chose them and left them to serve you.

sentences.zh: 愚以為宮中之事，事無大小，悉以咨之，然後施行，必能裨補闕漏，有所廣益。

translations.literal: Your servant thinks that in palace affairs, whether large or small, you should consult them on all and only then act—surely this will remedy omissions and bring broad benefit.
translations.idiomatic: I believe that in palace affairs, great or small, you should consult them on everything before acting. That will surely remedy gaps and bring real benefit.

sentences.zh: 將軍向寵，性行淑均，曉暢軍事，試用於昔日，先帝稱之曰能，是以眾議舉寵為督。

translations.literal: General Xiang Chong is even and fair in nature and conduct, well versed in military affairs; tested in former days, the late Emperor praised him as capable, and so by common counsel Chong was recommended as supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: General Xiang Chong is even-tempered and fair, and well versed in military affairs. The late Emperor tested him in earlier days and praised his ability, and so the court recommended him as camp supervisor.

sentences.zh: 愚以為營中之事，悉以咨之，必能使行陳和睦，優劣得所。

translations.literal: Your servant thinks that in camp affairs, if you consult him on all, you will surely make the ranks harmonious and assign merit and fault to their proper places.
translations.idiomatic: I believe that in camp affairs, if you consult him on everything, the ranks will stay harmonious and each man will be placed according to his worth.

sentences.zh: 「親賢臣，遠小人，此先漢所以興隆也；

translations.literal: "To draw near worthy ministers and keep petty men at a distance—this is why the Former Han flourished;
translations.idiomatic: "Draw worthy ministers close and keep petty men at a distance—that is why the Former Han rose to greatness;

sentences.zh: 親小人，遠賢臣，此後漢所以傾頹也。

translations.literal: to draw near petty men and keep worthy ministers at a distance—this is why the Later Han collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: draw petty men close and push worthy ministers away—that is why the Later Han fell into ruin.

sentences.zh: 先帝在時，每與臣論此事，未嘗不嘆息痛恨於桓、靈也。

translations.literal: When the late Emperor was alive, whenever he discussed this matter with your servant, he never failed to sigh and grieve with hatred over Emperors Huan and Ling.
translations.idiomatic: When the late Emperor was alive, he often discussed this with me, and never failed to sigh with grief and anger over Emperors Huan and Ling.

sentences.zh: 侍中、尚書、長史、參軍，此悉端良、死節之臣，願陛下親之，信之，則漢室之隆，可計日而待也。

translations.literal: Palace Attendants, Masters of Writing, Chief Clerks, and Staff Officers—these are all upright and good men, ministers who would die for their duty. I wish Your Majesty would draw them near and trust them; then the Han house's revival may be awaited by counting the days.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Attendants, Masters of Writing, Chief Clerks, and Staff Officers are all upright men who would die for their duty. If Your Majesty draws them close and trusts them, the revival of the Han house can be awaited by counting the days.

sentences.zh: 「臣本布衣，躬耕南陽，苟全性命於亂世，不求聞達於諸侯。

translations.literal: "Your servant was originally a commoner, tilling the fields himself in Nanyang, preserving life and limb in a chaotic age, seeking no fame or advancement among the lords.
translations.idiomatic: "I was once a commoner, farming in Nanyang, trying only to preserve my life in a chaotic age and seeking no fame among the warlords.

sentences.zh: 先帝不以臣卑鄙，猥自枉屈，三顧臣於草廬之中，咨臣以當世之事；

translations.literal: The late Emperor did not disdain your servant's lowliness, but condescended to humble himself, three times visiting your servant in a thatched hut and consulting your servant on affairs of the age;
translations.idiomatic: The late Emperor did not disdain my humble station. He humbled himself to visit me three times in my thatched hut and asked my counsel on the affairs of the age;

sentences.zh: 由是感激，遂許先帝以驅馳。

translations.literal: Moved by this, your servant then promised the late Emperor to serve at his command.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply moved, I then pledged myself to serve the late Emperor to the end.

sentences.zh: 後值傾覆，受任於敗軍之際，奉命於危難之間，爾來二十有一年矣。

translations.literal: Later came collapse; I received appointment amid defeated armies and took command in the midst of peril—twenty-one years have passed since then.
translations.idiomatic: Then came disaster. I was entrusted with office amid defeat and given command in the midst of peril. Twenty-one years have passed since then.

sentences.zh: 先帝知臣謹慎，故臨崩寄臣以大事也。

translations.literal: The late Emperor knew your servant was cautious, and so on his deathbed entrusted your servant with the great task.
translations.idiomatic: The late Emperor knew I was careful by nature, and so on his deathbed he entrusted me with the great task.

sentences.zh: 「受命以來，夙夜憂歎，恐托付不效，以傷先帝之明。

translations.literal: "Since receiving this charge, I have worried and sighed day and night, fearing the trust would not succeed and would wound the late Emperor's judgment.
translations.idiomatic: "Since receiving this charge, I have worried day and night, fearing that the trust placed in me might fail and tarnish the late Emperor's judgment.

sentences.zh: 故五月渡瀘，深入不毛。

translations.literal: Therefore in the fifth month I crossed the Lu River and penetrated deep into barren lands.
translations.idiomatic: That is why, in the fifth month, I crossed the Lu River and pushed deep into barren country.

sentences.zh: 今南方已定，甲兵已足，當獎率三軍，北定中原，庶竭駑鈍，攘除奸凶，興復漢室，還於舊都，此臣所以報先帝，而忠陛下之職分也。

translations.literal: Now the south is settled and armor and weapons are sufficient; I ought to encourage and lead the Three Armies north to settle the Central Plains, hoping to exhaust my dull talents, drive out the traitors and villains, restore the Han house, and return to the old capital—this is how your servant repays the late Emperor and fulfills loyalty to Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Now the south is settled and our arms are sufficient. I should encourage the Three Armies and march north to recover the Central Plains, doing all my limited powers allow to drive out the traitors, restore the Han house, and return to the old capital. That is how I repay the late Emperor and fulfill my duty to Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 至於斟酌損益，進盡忠言，則攸之、禕、允之任也。

translations.literal: As for weighing what to add or subtract and advancing fully loyal counsel, that is the responsibility of Youzhi, Yi, and Yun.
translations.idiomatic: As for weighing policy and offering forthright counsel, that is the duty of Youzhi, Yi, and Yun.

sentences.zh: 願陛下托臣以討賊興復之效，不效，則治臣之罪以告先帝之靈。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty would entrust your servant with the task of punishing the rebels and restoring the Han; if I fail, then punish your servant's crime to report to the late Emperor's spirit.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Your Majesty entrust me with the task of punishing the rebels and restoring the Han. If I fail, punish me as your law requires and report it to the late Emperor's spirit.

sentences.zh: 〔若無興德之言，則〕責攸之、禕、允等之慢以彰其咎<ref>〔若無興德之言則〕責攸之禕允等之慢以彰其咎據《三國志集解》引錢儀吉說補。

translations.literal: [If there are no words to promote virtue, then] hold Youzhi, Yi, Yun, and the like accountable for their negligence to make clear their fault<ref>[If there are no words to promote virtue then] hold Youzhi, Yi, Yun and the like accountable for their negligence to make clear their fault, supplied according to Qian Yiji's commentary cited in the Collected Exegesis of the Records of the Three Kingdoms.
translations.idiomatic: If there are no words to promote virtue, hold Youzhi, Yi, Yun, and the rest accountable for their negligence so their fault may be plain<ref>Supplied according to Qian Yiji's commentary cited in the Collected Exegesis of the Records of the Three Kingdoms.

sentences.zh: </ref>。

translations.literal: </ref>.
translations.idiomatic: End of editorial note.

sentences.zh: 陛下亦宜自謀，以諮諏善道，察納雅言，深追先帝遺詔。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should also plan for yourself, consult good paths, examine and accept refined words, and deeply follow the late Emperor's final charge.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should also think for yourself, seek good counsel, heed wise words, and hold fast to the late Emperor's final charge.

sentences.zh: 臣不勝受恩感激，今當遠離，臨表涕零，不知所言。

translations.literal: Your servant cannot bear the weight of received favor and is deeply moved; now about to depart far away, facing this memorial tears fall, and I know not what to say.
translations.idiomatic: I am overwhelmed with gratitude for your kindness. Now, as I prepare to depart, I weep over this memorial and scarcely know what more to say.

sentences.zh: 」遂行，屯於沔北陽平石馬。

translations.literal: " He then set out and encamped north of the Mian River at Yangping, Shima.
translations.idiomatic: " He then set out and encamped north of the Mian River at Yangping, Shima.

sentences.zh: 亮辟廣漢太守姚伷為掾，伷並進文武之士，亮稱之曰：「忠益者莫大於進人，進人者各務其所尚。

translations.literal: Liang recruited Administrator of Guanghan Yao You as a clerk; You together recommended men of civil and military talent, and Liang praised him, saying: "Nothing benefits loyalty more than recommending men; those who recommend men each pursue what they esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Liang recruited Yao You, Administrator of Guanghan, as a clerk. You recommended both civil and military men, and Liang praised him, saying, "Nothing serves loyalty better than recommending talent, and each recommender pursues what he most values.

sentences.zh: 今姚掾並存剛柔以廣文武之用，可謂博雅矣。

translations.literal: Now Clerk Yao preserves both firmness and flexibility to broaden use of civil and military men—this may be called broadly learned.
translations.idiomatic: Clerk Yao now keeps both firm and flexible men in view and broadens the use of civil and military talent. That may truly be called breadth of learning.

sentences.zh: 願諸掾各希此事以屬其望。

translations.literal: I wish all clerks would each aspire to this matter to fulfill their hopes.
translations.idiomatic: I hope every clerk will aspire to the same and live up to what is expected of him.

sentences.zh: 帝聞諸葛亮在漢中，欲大發兵就攻之，以問散騎常侍孫資，資曰：「昔武皇帝征南鄭，取張魯，陽平之役，危而後濟，又自往拔出夏侯淵軍，數言『南鄭直為天獄，中斜谷道為五百里石穴耳，』言其深險，喜出淵軍之辭也。

translations.literal: The Emperor heard that Zhuge Liang was at Hanzhong and wished to mobilize a great army to go attack him; he asked Regular Palace Attendant Sun Zi, and Zi said: "Formerly the Martial Emperor campaigned to Nanzheng and took Zhang Lu; at the battle of Yangping it was perilous before success was achieved, and he himself went to extricate Xiahou Yuan's army, repeatedly saying, 'Nanzheng is truly a heavenly prison, and the Zhong Slanting Valley road is merely a five-hundred-li stone cavern,' speaking of its depth and peril—words of joy at getting Yuan's army out.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor heard that Zhuge Liang was at Hanzhong, he wanted to mobilize a large army and attack him directly. He asked Regular Palace Attendant Sun Zi, who said, "The Martial Emperor once marched on Nanzheng to take Zhang Lu. At Yangping the battle was nearly lost before it was won, and he himself went to rescue Xiahou Yuan's army. He often said, 'Nanzheng is a prison made by heaven, and the Zhong Slanting Valley road is nothing but a five-hundred-li tunnel of stone,' speaking of its depth and danger—words spoken in relief at getting Yuan's army out alive.

sentences.zh: 又，武皇帝聖於用兵，察蜀賊棲於山巖，視吳虜竄於江湖，皆橈而避之，不責將士之力，不爭一朝之忿，誠所謂見勝而戰，知難而退也。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Martial Emperor was sage in the use of arms; seeing that Shu rebels dwelt in mountain cliffs and Wu enemies hid in rivers and lakes, he bent away and avoided them, not demanding the full strength of his generals and soldiers, not contending for a morning's anger—truly what is called fighting when victory is seen and withdrawing when difficulty is known.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Martial Emperor was masterful in war. Seeing that the Shu rebels held the mountain cliffs and the Wu enemy lurked on rivers and lakes, he bent aside and avoided them. He did not demand more of his officers and men than they could give, nor fight for a moment's anger. That was truly fighting when victory was in sight and withdrawing when the odds were against him.

sentences.zh: 今若進軍就南鄭討亮，道既險阻，計用精兵及轉運、鎮守南方四州，遏御水賊，凡用十五六萬人，必當復更有所發興。

translations.literal: If today we advance our army to Nanzheng to punish Liang, the road is already perilous and blocked; counting elite troops, transport, and garrison of the four southern provinces to check the river rebels, altogether some one hundred fifty to one hundred sixty thousand men would be used, and still more would surely have to be mobilized.
translations.idiomatic: If we now march on Nanzheng to attack Liang, the route is already perilous. Counting elite troops, supply transport, and garrisons in the four southern provinces to hold the river enemy at bay, we would need a hundred fifty or sixty thousand men at least, and still more would have to be raised.

sentences.zh: 天下騷動，費力廣大，此誠陛下所宜深慮。

translations.literal: The realm would be shaken, the cost vast—this is truly what Your Majesty ought to consider deeply.
translations.idiomatic: The realm would be thrown into turmoil and the cost would be enormous. Your Majesty should weigh that carefully.

sentences.zh: 夫守戰之力，力役參倍。

translations.literal: As for the strength of defense versus offense, labor and service are two or three times greater.
translations.idiomatic: Defense and offense are not equal: the labor required for war is two or three times greater.

sentences.zh: 但以今日見兵分命大將據諸要險，威足以震攝強寇，鎮靜疆場，將士虎睡，百姓無事。

translations.literal: But if with today's existing troops you assign great generals to hold the key passes, your authority will suffice to awe strong invaders, calm the borders, let officers and soldiers sleep like tigers, and leave the people untroubled.
translations.idiomatic: But if you divide the forces you already have and place great generals at the key passes, your authority will be enough to overawe strong enemies, keep the borders quiet, let your officers and men rest like tigers at ease, and leave the people undisturbed.

sentences.zh: 數年之間，中國日盛，吳、蜀二虜必自罷敝。

translations.literal: Within a few years, the Central Realm will daily grow stronger, and the two enemies Wu and Shu will surely wear themselves out on their own.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years the Central Realm will grow stronger day by day, and the two enemies, Wu and Shu, will wear themselves out on their own.

sentences.zh: 」帝乃止。

translations.literal: " The Emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor then abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 4初，文帝罷五銖錢，使以穀帛為用，人間巧偽漸多，競濕穀以要利，薄絹以為市，雖處以嚴刑，不能禁也。

translations.literal: 4. Earlier, Emperor Wen abolished the five-shu coin and had grain and silk used as currency; among the people clever counterfeiting gradually increased, competing to dampen grain for profit and thin silk for market exchange—even with severe punishments it could not be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: 4. Earlier, Emperor Wen had abolished the five-shu coin and ordered grain and silk to serve as currency. Counterfeiting spread among the people: grain was dampened for profit and silk was thinned for trade. Even severe punishment could not stop it.

sentences.zh: 司馬芝等舉朝大議，以為：「用錢非徒豐國，亦所以省刑，今不若更鑄五銖為便。

translations.literal: Sima Zhi and others raised a great court debate, holding: "Using coin not only enriches the state but also reduces punishments; today it would be better to recast the five-shu coin.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhi and others raised the matter in full court debate, arguing, "Coinage not only enriches the state but also reduces crime. It would be better to recast the five-shu coin.

sentences.zh: 」夏，四月，乙亥，復行五銖錢。

translations.literal: " In summer, fourth month, on the day Yihai, the five-shu coin was restored.
translations.idiomatic: " In summer, in the fourth month, on the day Yihai, the five-shu coin was restored.

sentences.zh: 5甲申，初營宗廟於洛陽。

translations.literal: 5. On the day Jiashen, the ancestral temple was first built at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: 5. On the day Jiashen, construction of the ancestral temple at Luoyang began.

sentences.zh: 6六月，以司馬懿都督荊、豫州諸軍事，率所領鎮宛。

translations.literal: 6. Sixth month, Sima Yi was made Area Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in Jing and Yu provinces, leading the forces under his command to garrison Wan.
translations.idiomatic: 6. In the sixth month, Sima Yi was made area commander-in-chief of all military affairs in Jing and Yu provinces and led his forces to garrison Wan.

sentences.zh: 7冬，十二月，立貴嬪河內毛氏為皇后。

translations.literal: 7. Winter, twelfth month, Honored Consort Lady Mao of Henei was established as Empress.
translations.idiomatic: 7. In winter, in the twelfth month, Honored Consort Lady Mao of Henei was made Empress.

sentences.zh: 初，帝為平原王，納河內虞氏為妃；

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Emperor was Prince of Pingyuan, he took Lady Yu of Henei as consort;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Emperor was Prince of Pingyuan, he had taken Lady Yu of Henei as his consort;

sentences.zh: 及即位，虞氏不得立為後，太皇卞太后慰勉焉。

translations.literal: when he ascended the throne, Lady Yu could not be established as Empress, and Grand Empress Dowager Lady Bian comforted and encouraged her.
translations.idiomatic: but when he took the throne, Lady Yu was not made Empress. Grand Empress Dowager Lady Bian comforted her.

sentences.zh: 虞氏曰：「曹氏自好立賤，未有能以義舉者也。

translations.literal: Lady Yu said: "The Cao house has always favored elevating the lowly, yet none have ever been raised by righteous principle.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yu said, "The house of Cao has always liked to elevate the lowborn, yet none of them have ever been raised on grounds of merit.

sentences.zh: 然後職內事，君聽外政，其道相由而成；

translations.literal: Yet afterward the wife manages inner affairs and the husband hears outer governance—their way is mutually achieved;
translations.idiomatic: Still, the wife governs within and the husband governs without, and the two roles must work together;

sentences.zh: 苟不能以善始，未有能令終者也，殆必由此亡國喪祀矣！

translations.literal: if one cannot begin well, there has never been one who could finish well—likely from this the state will perish and the sacrifices be lost!
translations.idiomatic: if a reign cannot begin rightly, it has never ended well. The dynasty will likely perish and its ancestral rites be cut off because of this!

sentences.zh: 」虞氏遂絀還鄴宮。

translations.literal: " Lady Yu then withdrew in disgrace and returned to the palace at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: " Lady Yu then withdrew in disgrace and returned to the palace at Ye.

sentences.zh: 8初，太祖、世祖皆議復肉刑，以軍事不果。

translations.literal: 8. Earlier, the Founding Emperor and the Martial Emperor both debated restoring corporal punishment, but because of military affairs it was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: 8. Earlier, both the Founding Emperor and the Martial Emperor had debated restoring corporal punishment, but war had prevented it.

sentences.zh: 及帝即位，太傅鐘繇上言：「宜如孝景之令，其當棄市欲斬右趾者，許之；

translations.literal: When the Emperor took the throne, Grand Tutor Zhong Yao submitted a memorial: "It is fitting to follow the ordinance of Emperor Xiaojing: for those who deserve execution by market display but are to have the right foot cut off instead, permit it;
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor took the throne, Grand Tutor Zhong Yao submitted a memorial arguing, "We should follow Emperor Xiaojing's ordinance: for those condemned to execution by market display who may instead have the right foot cut off, permit it;

sentences.zh: 其黥、劓、左趾、官刑者，自如孝文易以髡笞，可以歲生三千人。

translations.literal: for tattooing, nose-cutting, left-foot cutting, and castration, as under Emperor Xiaowen replace them with shaving and flogging—by this three thousand persons may be saved each year.
translations.idiomatic: for tattooing, nose-cutting, left-foot amputation, and castration, follow Emperor Xiaowen's practice of replacing them with shaving and flogging. By this, three thousand lives could be saved each year.

sentences.zh: 」詔公卿以下議，司徒朗以為：「肉刑不用已來，歷年數百；

translations.literal: " An edict ordered discussion among the Three Dukes and ministers below; Minister of Works Lang held: "Since corporal punishment ceased to be used, several hundred years have passed;
translations.idiomatic: " An edict ordered the Three Dukes and all ministers below to debate the matter. Minister of Works Lang argued, "Corporal punishment has not been used for several hundred years;

sentences.zh: 今復行之，恐所減之文未彰於萬民之目，而肉刑之問已宣於寇讎之耳，非所以來遠人也。

translations.literal: if it is restored now, I fear the leniency of the reduced punishments has not yet been displayed before the eyes of the myriad people, while inquiry into corporal punishment will already be proclaimed in the ears of enemy foes—this is not the way to win over those afar.
translations.idiomatic: if we restore it now, I fear the mercy of our reduced punishments has not yet been plain to the people, while word of corporal punishment will already reach our enemies. That is no way to win over distant peoples.

sentences.zh: 今可按繇所欲輕之死罪，使減死髡刑，嫌其輕者，可倍其居作之歲數。

translations.literal: Today we may follow what Yao wishes and lighten capital crimes, making commuted death into shaving punishment; for those who find it too light, their years of penal labor may be doubled.
translations.idiomatic: We could instead follow Yao's aim by lightening capital crimes, commuting death to shaving and flogging, and doubling the years of penal labor for those who find the penalty too lenient.

sentences.zh: 內有以生易死不訾之恩，外無以刖易釱駭耳之聲。

translations.literal: Within, there would be the grace of exchanging death for life without reproach; without, there would be no sound of mutilation exchanged for shackles to startle the ears.
translations.idiomatic: Within the realm, men would receive the grace of life instead of death without reproach; abroad, there would be no rumor of mutilation and shackling to alarm men's ears.

sentences.zh: 」議者百餘人，與朗同者多。

translations.literal: " More than a hundred who deliberated agreed with Lang.
translations.idiomatic: " More than a hundred debaters took Lang's side.

sentences.zh: 9是歲，吳昭武將軍韓當卒，其子綜淫亂不軌，懼得罪，閏月，將其家屬、部曲來奔。

translations.literal: 9. This year Wu General Who Establishes Martial Might Han Dang died; his son Zong was licentious and disorderly, feared punishment, and in the intercalary month led his household and retainers to defect.
translations.idiomatic: 9. That year Han Dang, Wu's General Who Establishes Martial Might, died. His son Zong, dissolute and lawless, feared punishment and in the intercalary month fled to Wei with his family and troops.

sentences.zh: 10初，孟達既為文帝所寵，又與桓階、夏侯尚親善；

translations.literal: 10. Earlier Meng Da had been favored by Emperor Wen and was also on intimate terms with Huan Jie and Xiahou Shang;
translations.idiomatic: 10. Earlier Meng Da had won Emperor Wen's favor and was close to Huan Jie and Xiahou Shang;

sentences.zh: 及文帝殂，階、尚皆卒，達心不自安。

translations.literal: when Emperor Wen died, Jie and Shang both passed away, and Da's heart was not at ease.
translations.idiomatic: when Wen died and Jie and Shang followed him to the grave, Da grew uneasy.

sentences.zh: 達與魏興太守申儀有隙，儀密表告之。

translations.literal: Da had a rift with Administrator of Weixing Shen Yi; Yi secretly memorialized to report this.
translations.idiomatic: Da feuded with Shen Yi, prefect of Weixing, who secretly reported him to the throne.

sentences.zh: 達聞之，惶懼，欲舉兵叛。

translations.literal: When Da heard of it, he was fearful and wished to raise troops in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Da heard this, panicked, and prepared to rebel.

sentences.zh: 司馬懿以書慰解之，達猶豫未決，懿乃潛軍進討。

translations.literal: Sima Yi sent a letter to soothe and reassure him; Da hesitated and could not decide, and Yi then secretly advanced troops to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi wrote to reassure him, but while Da still wavered Yi marched in secret to attack.

sentences.zh: 諸將言達與吳、漢交通，宜觀望而後動。

translations.literal: The generals said Da was in communication with Wu and Han and that one should observe and wait before acting.
translations.idiomatic: His officers urged caution, saying Da was in touch with Wu and Han and they should wait before moving.

sentences.zh: 懿曰：「達無信義，此其相疑之時也。

translations.literal: Yi said: "Da has no faith or righteousness—this is the moment when mutual suspicion arises.
translations.idiomatic: Yi said: "Da is faithless—this is the hour of mutual suspicion.

sentences.zh: 當及其未定促決之。

translations.literal: We should press for a decision while he is still unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: Strike while he is still undecided.

sentences.zh: 」乃倍道兼行，八日到其城下。

translations.literal: " He then marched by double stages day and night and in eight days reached beneath his walls.
translations.idiomatic: He forced the march day and night and reached the city in eight days.

sentences.zh: 吳、漢各遣偏將向西城安橋、木闌塞以救達，懿分諸將以距之。

translations.literal: Wu and Han each sent subordinate generals toward Xicheng, Anqiao, and Mulansai to rescue Da; Yi divided his generals to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: Wu and Han each sent detachments toward Xicheng, Anqiao, and Mulansai to relieve Da; Yi detached commanders to block them.

sentences.zh: 初，達與亮書曰：「宛去洛八百里，去吾一千二百里。

translations.literal: Earlier Da wrote to Liang: "Wan is eight hundred li from Luoyang and twelve hundred li from me.
translations.idiomatic: Da had written to Liang: "Wan lies eight hundred li from Luoyang and twelve hundred from me.

sentences.zh: 聞吾舉事，當表上天子，比相反覆，一月間也，則吾城已固，諸軍足辦。

translations.literal: When you hear that I have risen, you will memorialize the Son of Heaven; by the time reports go back and forth, a month will have passed, and my city will already be secure and the armies sufficient to deal with matters.
translations.idiomatic: When I rise, word must reach the Son of Heaven and return—a month at least—by which time my walls will stand firm and my troops be ready.

sentences.zh: 吾所在深險，司馬公必不自來；

translations.literal: Where I am is deep and perilous; Lord Sima is sure not to come in person;
translations.idiomatic: My post lies in deep country; Lord Sima will never come himself;

sentences.zh: 諸將來，吾無患矣。

translations.literal: if the generals come, I have no worries.
translations.idiomatic: if only his generals come, I have nothing to fear.

sentences.zh: 」及兵到，達又告亮曰：「吾舉事八日而兵至城下，何其神速也！

translations.literal: " When the troops arrived, Da again informed Liang: "I rose in arms eight days ago and the army is already beneath my walls—how swift!
translations.idiomatic: When the army came, Da wrote Liang again: "I rebelled eight days ago and they are already at my walls—how fast they move!
